GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3000 
TO BE ANSWERED ON AUGUST 06, 2026 
 
NAMO BHARAT REGIONAL RAPID TRANSIT SYSTEM 
NO. 3000 DR. HEMANG JOSHI: 
    SHRI PRADEEP KUMAR SINGH: 
  SHRI ARUN GOVIL: 
  SHRI JANARDAN MISHRA: 
  SHRI MANISH JAISWAL:  
 
 Will the Minister of HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) the details of  the milestones achieved under the Namo Bharat 
Regional Rapid Transit System  (RRTS), particularly following the full 
operationalisation of the 82- kilometre Delhi-Ghaziabad-Meerut corridor 
in February, 2026;  
(b) the details of the current ridership metrics and punctuality standards 
including the framework for multimodal convergence with existing 
metro networks and bus terminals to facilitate seamless commuter 
mobility; 
(c) the details of the current status and projected roadmap for  the 
subsequent Phase- I corridors and the proposed linkage to Jewar 
Airport to ensure interoperable regional connectivity; and 
(d) the details of the specific interventions implemented by the National 
Capital Region Transport Corporation (NCRTC) to foster transit -
oriented development, integrate renewable energy solutions and 
provide inclusive fare structures for marginalised categories?   
 
ANSWER 
       THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE 
 MINISTRY OF HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS 
     (SHRI TOKHAN SAHU) 
 
(a): The 82.15 Km long India’s first Namo Bharat Regional Rapid 
Transit System (RRTS) corridor namely, Delhi -Ghaziabad-Meerut RRTS 
corridor (which includes 23 km of Meerut metro network on same 
infrastructure) has become fully operational since February, 2026.  
  
…2/- 
 
 
 

-2- 
(b): National Capital Region Transport Corporation Ltd. (NCRTC), the 
implementing agency for Namo Bharat RRTS, has informed that as on 
date, over 3.8 crores commuters have availed the Namo Bharat services 
since beginning of operation with a punctuality level of over 99%. Further, 
on Delhi -Ghaziabad-Meerut Namo Bharat RRTS corridor, effective multi -
modal integration has been established with 03 Metro lines, 02 Railway 
stations and 04 Bus terminals , conforming to the guidelines outlined by 
Unified Traffic and Transportation Infrastructure (Planning and 
Engineering) Centre, DDA. 
 
(c): In Phase- I, three Namo Bharat RRTS corridors have been 
prioritized namely, (i) Delhi -Ghaziabad-Meerut, (ii) Delhi -Gurugram-Alwar 
and (iii) Delhi -Panipat. The Delhi -Ghaziabad-Meerut Namo Bharat RRTS 
corridor is fully operational since February, 2026. Further, NCRTC has 
submitted the Detailed Project Reports (DPRs) for the Namo Bharat RRTS 
corridors from Delhi to Karnal, Delhi to Bawal, Bawal to Behror and 
Ghaziabad to Noida International Airport. The Namo Bharat RRTS projects 
are cost intensive proposals and therefore, undergo intensive 
examination at different levels in Central Government. After such 
examination, Central Government considers financial assistance to RRTS 
projects, based on feasibility of the proposal and availability of resources. 
 
(d): NCRTC has informed that it has implemented several specific 
interventions across the Delhi -Ghaziabad-Meerut Namo Bharat RRTS 
corridor, such as, (i) TOD Zones of the Delhi -Ghaziabad-Meerut have been 
delineated and notified in Masterplans of Ghaziabad and Meerut along 
with special areas for TOD, (ii) Under Delhi TOD policy, 2021, NCRTC has 
prepared Influence Zone Plans (IZP) for the TOD Nodes at Jangpura and 
Sarai Kale Khan. Further, as per provisions of Delhi TOD Policy, 2026, any 
new RRTS corridor will automatically be considered under TOD in Delhi. 
NCRTC has further informed that a cumulative rooftop solar capacity of 
7.8 MWp has been successfully installed to harness green energy. In 
respect of fare structure, NCRTC has informed that a 35% discount on 
base fare is being provided to all commuters. Additionally, NCRTC has 
also introduced concept of loyalty points, which are earned by commuters 
by traveling on RRTS network, which is used for availing discount.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
  
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3001 
ANSWERED ON 6TH AUGUST, 2026 
  
WIDENING OF AROOR TO EDAPPALLY STRETCH ON NH-66 
  
3001. SHRI HIBI EDEN: 
  
Will the Minister of ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
सड़क परिवहन औि िाजमार्ग मंत्री  
be pleased to state:  
  
(a) whether the Government proposes an eight -lane elevated highway on the 
Aroor to Edappally stretch of National Highway (NH)-66; 
  
(b) if  so, the details and the present status thereof and if not, the reasons 
therefor; 
  
(c) whether the Aroor to Edappally stretch of NH -66 is among the most 
congested National Highway stretches in Kerala and if so, the comparative 
traffic data thereof; 
  
(d) whether there are any alternative arrangements proposed to address the 
severe traffic congestion on the Aroor to Edappally stretch of NH -66, which 
has multiple major junctions and crossings of the Kochi Metro corridor, if so, 
the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor; and 
  
(e) whether the Aroor to Edappally stretch of NH -66 in Kerala is the only 
National Highway stretch without a clear decision or timeline from the 
Government, if so, the details thereof? 
  
  

ANSWER 
  
THE MINISTER OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
 
(SHRI NITIN JAIRAM GADKARI) 
  
(a) to (e)    Government keeps on undertaking Detailed Project Report (DPR)/ 
feasibility study to upgrade the National Highway (NH) network   with the aim 
to improve logistic efficiency and reduce the travel time.  The existing 4-lane 
carriageway on Aroor –Edappally stretch of NH -66 accommodates Kochi 
Metro Corridor. In order to address traffic congestion in this stretch, which 
passes through busy locations such as Angamaly, Aluva, Kalamassery, 
Edappally, Palarivattom, Vyttila and Kundannoor  in Ernakulam district, work 
of DPR for Ernakulam Bypass (Kochi Outer Ring Road)   has been awarded, 
connecting Angamaly (near Cochin International Airport) to Aroor. The 
alignment of the said project was approved in the meeting of the Alignment 
Approval Committee (AAC). Decision for project implementation and 
investment is taken based on the outcome of DPR and compliance with the 
Policy for decongestion of urban areas issued on 29th May, 2026.

3002.  SHRI MANISH JAISWAL: 
SHRI MANOJ TIWARI: 
SHRI VIJAY BAGHEL: 
SHRI BHARTRUHARI MAHTAB: 
SHRI P P CHAUDHARY: 
SHRI DILIP SAIKIA:

DR. MANNA LAL RAWAT: 
SHRI JASHUBHAI BHILUBHAI RATHVA: 
SHRI KOTA SRINIVASA POOJARY: 
SMT. ANITA NAGARSINGH CHOUHAN: 
SHRI MAHENDRA SINGH SOLANKY: 
SHRI RAHUL SINGH LODHI: 
SHRI JANARDAN MISHRA: 
SHRI RAJKUMAR CHAHAR: 
SHRI KRISHNA PRASAD TENNETI: 
DR. SANJAY JAISWAL: 
SHRI CHAVDA VINOD LAKHAMSHI: 
SHRI CHANDRA PRAKASH CHOUDHARY 
 
पेĚोͧलयम और Ĥाकृ Ǔतक गैस मंğी 
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has reviewed the progress of the National Gas Grid and 
associated natural gas pipeline network across the country, if so, the details thereof including its 
present length, State-wise and in Dewas-Shajapur Parliamentary Constituency; 
 
(b) the details of natural gas pipeline projects sanctioned/under implementation/operational 
under the National Gas Grid and the progress made in expanding pipeline connectivity in the 
country and to previously unconnected regions, districts and industrial clusters, particularly in 
Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Jharkhand and the Pali Parliamentary Constituency; 
 
(c) whether the Government has taken/proposes to take measures to expedite ongoing 
pipeline projects, strengthen inter-State connectivity, expand City Gas Distribution (CGD) 
infrastructure including Piped Natural Gas (PNG) and Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) facilities 
particularly in above States and in Delhi especially in North-East Delhi, the Ratlam–Jhabua– 
Alirajpur and Dewas–Shajapur Parliamentary Constituencies in view of its importance for 
Tribal/Industrial development in Madhya Pradesh along with the timeline, funds allocated and any 
special plan therein, if so, the details thereof; and 
 
(d) the expected impact of the expansion of the National Gas Grid and CGD network on 
industrial growth, clean energy adoption, employment generation, natural gas accessibility and 
the development of a gas-based economy in the country? 
 
ANSWER 
पेĚोͧलयम और Ĥाकृ Ǔतक गैस मंğालय मɅ राÏय मंğी 
(Įी सुरेश गोपी )   
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS 
(SHRI SURESH GOPI) 

(a) to (d) Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board (PNGRB) is the authority to grant authorization to 
various entities to Lay, build, operate and expand Natural Gas Pipelines (NGPL). As on March 2026, 
PNGRB has authorized approximately 33,027 Km of common carrier natural gas pipeline across the 
country to create a National Gas Grid. All the States and Union Territories, except Ladakh, Andaman & 
Nicobar Island and Lakshwadeep are covered by Natural Gas Pipeline Network authorized by PNGRB.  
The details of the Common Carrier Natural Gas Pipeline network including the States of Madhya Pradesh, 
Rajasthan, and Jharkhand are enclosed as Annexure-I. In the Dewas - Shajapur Parliamentary Constituency 
of Madhya Pradesh, approximately 84.67 km of operational natural gas pipeline network is deployed under 
the National Gas Grid. This operational infrastructure comprises major trunk and spur lines, including 
sections of Hazira - Vijaipur (24.91 km), Dahej - Vijaipur (DVPL I) (24.93 km), Dahej - Vijaipur (DVPL II) 
(24.95 km), Sanwer - Dewas (8.52 km), Dewas - HR Johnson (1.30 km), and the HR Johnson - Roca spur 
line (0.07 km), providing robust natural gas connectivity across the constituency.  
Providing Piped Natural Gas (PNG) connections and establishment of Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) 
stations is part of the development of City Gas Distribution (CGD) Network, which inter alia include 
creation of pipeline infrastructure and other facilities for the supply of PNG to domestic, commercial and 
industrial units and CNG to transport sector which is being carried out by the entities authorized by 
Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board (PNGRB). PNGRB has authorized entities for the 
development of CGD network in 309 Geographical Areas (GAs), covering the entire mainland area of the 
country. Details of CGD progress in the states of Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan and Jharkhand and CGD 
progress in the Pali Parliamentary Constituency, North-East Delhi, Ratlam and Jhabua Districts, Alirajpur 
District, Dewas District and Shajapur District are given at Annexure – II. 
No funds are sanctioned or allocated by Government for implementation of the CGD projects. The CGD 
infrastructure rollout and investmentsare made by the authorized CGD entity in accordance with the 
authorization granted by PNGRB and the approved project plan. 
Government have taken various steps to expand access to natural gas to CNG (Transport)/ PNG (Domestic) 
sector in the country which inter-alia includes allocating domestic gas on priority basis, diverting domestic 
gas from non-priority sectors to meet requirement for CNG (T)/PNG(D) sector, expansion of CGD network, 
grant of public utility status to CGD projects, notification for supply of domestic gas through available 
mode (including cascade mode) for CNG(T)/PNG(D) purpose, allocating domestic natural gas for CNG(T) 
and PNG(D) segments on a two quarter advance basis, expansion of National Gas Grid Pipeline, setting up 
of Liquefied Natural Gas (LNG) Terminals, Sustainable Alternative Towards Affordable Transportation 
(SATAT) initiatives to promote Bio-CNG, etc.  
PNGRB in collaboration with CGD entities, launched the National PNG Drive 2.0 from 1st January, 2026 to 
30th June, 2026. Under the initiatives various measures have been implemented by the Government and 
authorized CGD entities which include: 
(i) Expansion of PNG connectivity to households, commercial establishments and industries; 
(ii) Conversion of connected households into active billed consumers; 
(iii) Awareness campaigns and consumer outreach programmes; 
(iv) Coordination with State Governments and local authorities for expeditious statutory 
permissions; and 
(v) Implementation of consumer-friendly measures, including digital registration, simplified 
connection processes and promotional schemes offered by CGD entities. 
Government has also notified a comprehensive control order dated 24.03.2026 under the Essential 
Commodities Act, 1955 to facilitate time-bound expansion of pipeline infrastructure across the country, 
especially CGD. The order provides a uniform framework for grant of right of way (RoW) and permissions 

by mandating strict timelines, enabling deemed approvals in case of delays, and prohibiting imposition of 
unauthorized charges by public authorities. It also addresses access issues in residential and private areas by 
ensuring non-discriminatory and time-bound permissions, thereby removing key bottlenecks in pipeline 
laying. 
PNGRB has rationalized the Unified Tariff by reducing tariff zones from three to two and notified 
transportation tariffs of Rs. 54.00/MMBTU for Zone-1 (up to 300 Km) and Rs. 110.02/MMBTU for Zone-2 
(beyond 300 Km), . Zone-1 tariff has been extended nationwide for CNG(T) and PNG(D), resulting in 
nearly 50% reduction in transportation charges for consumers beyond 300 Km.  
The expansion of the natural gas pipeline grid has significantly improved access of natural gas for City Gas 
Distribution (CGD) networks, industries, power plants and households. As on 31.05.2026, the number of 
PNG Domestic connections has registered a substantial increase from 22 lakh in 2013-14 to approx.170 lakh 
currently, while the network of CNG stations has expanded from 783in 2013-14 to more than 8,900 
currently. Furthermore, authorized entities have laid 6,71,387 Inch-Km pipeline across the country and 
provided 22,256 Industrial and 52,143 Commercial connections to support the clean energy transition in 
their respective Geographical Areas. 
The expansion of the natural gas pipeline grid across the country has significantly increased adoption of 
natural gas which has played a crucial role in reducing India’s dependence on conventional fossil fuels like 
coal and crude oil. Consumption of Natural Gas in the country has increased 
from approx 138 Million Metric Standard Cubic Meters per Day (MMSCMD) in 2014 to approx. 188 
MMSCMD in 2025. With expanding pipeline and CGD network, use of CNG as transportation fuel in 
vehicles (due to its cost effectiveness and lower emissions) is increasing. Similarly, industries previously 
dependent on furnace oil and diesel are also progressively shifting to natural gas (mainly in the form of 
piped natural gas). Further, expansion of CGD infrastructure generates both direct and indirect employment 
opportunities through construction, operations, maintenance and allied services thereby supporting local 
employment and self-employment and leading to the development of a gas based economy.

LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION No. 3003 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 6th August, 2026 
PROMOTION OF SUSTAINABLE AVIATION FUEL 
 
 
3003.  SHRI DARSHAN SINGH CHOUDHARY 
 पेĚोͧलयम और Ĥाकृ Ǔतक गैस मंğी  
 
 Will the Minister of PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has implemented any special policy, incentive scheme or action plan 
during the year 2026 to promote the production, use and supply of Sustainable Aviation Fuel 
(SAF), if so, the details thereof; 
(b) whether the Government is taking any special initiative in collaboration with Oil Marketing 
Companies, aviation companies, research institutions and the private sector to enhance the 
production capacity, blending, quality standards and supply chain of SAF for increasing its use 
in the aviation sector, if so, the details thereof; 
(c) the details of the pilot projects approved, research and development activities, investments, 
production capacity and financial assistance relating to SAF during the year 2026; and 
(d) whether the Government is implementing any time-bound action plan to promote the 
indigenous production of SAF from agricultural residues, used cooking oil, bio-waste and other 
bio-based feedstocks with a view to reducing dependence on imported aviation fuel and 
lowering carbon emissions, if so, the details thereof? 
ANSWER 
पेᮝोिलयम और ᮧाक ृ ितक गैस मंᮢालय मᱶ रा᭔य मंᮢी 
(᮰ी सुरेश गोपी) 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM & NATURAL GAS  
 (SHRI SURESH GOPI) 
(a) to (d): The Government has approved indicative blending targets of 1% by 2027, 2% by 2028, 
and 5% by 2030 for Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) in conventional Aviation Turbine Fuel (ATF),  
initially for international flights. Public sector Oil Marketing Companies are actively engaged in 
achieving the stated blending targets.  
 
Further, the Government has taken several steps to support the development of a SAF ecosystem in the 
country. These include: 
 
(i) Notification of amendment to the Aviation Turbine Fuel (ATF) (Regulation of Marketing) 
Order, 2001 (ATF Control Order) vide notification dated 17 April 2026, as an 
administrative measure to bring Aviation Turbine Fuel blended with Sustainable Aviation 
Fuel (SAF) under the ambit of the ATF Control Order. 
(ii) Recognition of the National Accreditation Board for Certification Bodies (NABCB) for 
accreditation of SAF certification bodies under the International Sustainability and Carbon 
Certification (ISCC) scheme. 

(iii)  Facilitation of long-term SAF supply arrangements between Oil Marketing Companies 
(OMCs) and airlines, including the signing of Memoranda of Understanding between 
OMCs and Airlines, 
(iv) Conducting stakeholder consultations and awareness programmes on SAF. 
 
Indian Oil Corporation limited (IOCL) and Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited (BPCL) have 
received ISCC Carbon Offsetting and Reduction Scheme for International Aviation (ISCC CORSIA) 
certification for SAF production at their Panipat and Mumbai refineries, respectively.  
 
To facilitate Advanced Biofuel production including SAF, the Government notified the "Pradhan 
Mantri JI- V AN (Jaiv Indhan- Vatavaran Anukool Fasal Awashesh Nivaran) Yojana" in 2019, amended 
in 2024, with the objectives to establish advanced biofuels projects including projects for SAF 
production in the country using lignocellulosic biomass and other renewable feedstocks. The total 
financial outlay for PM JI-V AN is Rs. 1,969.50 crore, of which Rs. 1,800 crore is allocated for 
commercial-scale advanced biofuel projects and Rs. 150 crore for demonstration- scale advanced 
biofuel projects. The total cost of the project inter-alia includes biomass supply chain and handling, 
technology charges, cost of the total equipment etc. Under the PM JI-V AN Yojana, the maximum 
financial assistance of Rs.150 crore per project for commercial scale projects and Rs. 15 crore per 
project for demonstration scale projects have been prescribed for improving commercial viability as 
well as promoting R&D for development and adoption of technologies in the field of production of 
advanced biofuels. 
 
In June 2026, financial assistance was approved under the PM JI-V AN Yojana for three commercial-

MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. : 3004 
 ( TO BE ANSWERED ON THE  6th August 2026 )  
DEVELOPMENT OF AVIATION SECTOR UNDER UDAN SCHEME  
3004.    SHRI MALAIYARASAN D                      
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION 
be pleased to state:- 
(a) the details and the current status of implementation of the Ude Desh ka Aam 
Nagrik (UDAN) scheme including the number of routes operationalised, 
airports/heliports/water aerodromes made functional, State/UT-wise, particularly in 
Kallakurichi Lok Sabha Constituency of Tamil Nadu; 
(b) the total funds allocated, released and utilised under the said scheme since its 
inception till date, year-wise; 
(c) whether several regional routes have been discontinued or suspended du e to 
low passenger traffic or financial viability issues and if so, the details thereof; 
(d) the steps taken to improve last-mile air connectivity in remote, hilly and coastal 
regions and to ensure long-term sustainability of subsidised routes; and 
(e) whether the Government proposes any modification or extension of the UDAN 
Scheme beyond its current phase and if so, the details thereof? 
ANSWER 
Minister of State in the Ministry of CIVIL AVIATION      (Shri Murlidhar Mohol) 
(a) to (e): Since inception of the  Regional Connectivity Scheme (RCS) -UDAN, a 
total of 679 RCS routes connecting 95 unserved and underserved airports, 
including 17 heliports and 02 water aerodromes, have been operationalised across 
the country under the UDAN Scheme. 
No aerodromes located in the Kallakurichi Lok Sabha Constituency of Tamil Nadu 
have been identified for development under the UDAN Scheme. 
For revival and development of un -served and under -served 
airports/heliports/water aerodromes identified under Regional Connectivity 
Scheme - Ude Desh ka Aam Nagrik (RCS-UDAN), an amount of Rs. 4500 crore in 
the Phase I and an amount of Rs.1000 Crores in Phase II of the Scheme has been 

allocated. Rs.4,839.48 crore has been incurred for revival/development of airports 
under RCS till date. 
Under the scheme, 156 routes discontinued services before completion of their 3 -
year VGF support tenure due to operational and airline related issues. 
The next phase of the UDAN Scheme was launched on 04.07.2026 to promote 
regional air connectivity in Tier 2 an d Tier 3 cities and remote regions across the 
country, targeting 120 new destinations and 4 crore passengers over the next 10 
years. The Scheme is being implemented from FY 2026 -27 to FY 2035-36 with an 
outlay of Rs 28,840 crore, including Rs. 12,159 crore  for Aerodrome development 
and Rs3,661 crore for development of 200 heliports in Hilly, North -Eastern and 
Aspirational (HINER) States/districts.

3006. SHRI SUKHJINDER SINGH RANDHAWA:

Will the Minister of ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
  
सड़क परिवहन औि िाजमार्ग मंत्री 
  
be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has reviewed the implementation of the 
Bhoomi Rashi Portal for land acquisition under National Highway (NH) 
projects, if so, the details thereof, State/UT-wise; 
  

(b) the details of land acquired, affected farmers/landowners and 
compensation paid to them  through the said portal, State -wise and 
district-wise; 
  
(c) the details of the progress made in digitisation of the land 
acquisition process and direct  disbursement of compensation through 
the portal and the present status thereof, State/UT -wise particularly in 
Punjab; 
  
(d) whether any special measures and  the steps have been taken to 
improve transparency,  reduce delays in land acquisition, resolve 
pending cases and address grievances of farmers  under National 
Highway projects, if so, the details thereof, State/UT-wise; 
  
(e) the impact of the said portal o n expediting project implementation, 
ensuring transparency  and improving timely disbursement of 
compensation to affected landowners, State/UT-wise; and 
  
(f) the details of ongoing and upcoming NH infrastructure project, 
State/UT-wise? 
  
ANSWER 
  
THE MINISTER OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
  
(SHRI NITIN JAIRAM GADKARI) 
  
(a) to (e)    The BhoomiRashi Portal is a centrally monitored portal and 
its development is regularly reviewed by the Central Government in 
Ministry of Road Transport and Highways. 
  
The intent of BhoomiRashi Portal is to provide single -point 
platform for online processing of notifications related to land 
acquisition under the National Highways (NH) Act, 1956 to accelerate 
highway infrastructure development projects in India and 

disbursement of the compensation to the recipient. The Portal has 
been made mandatory for processing land acquisition notifications. 
The Portal was launched for the said purposes in April 2018. The 
Portal supports the plotting of GIS -based acquisition maps, and h as 
been integrated with Public Financial Management System (PFMS) and 
Aadhaar-based authentication to improve accuracy and reliability in 
disbursement of compensation to land owners. The BhoomiRashi 
Portal through its online processing has reduced the aver age time 
taken for statutory notifications. 
  
          The land acquisition for National Highway projects is project -
based and a continuous process. The Competent Authority for Land 
Acquisition (CALA) is responsible for the preparation of the awards. 
The total land acquired through BhoomiRashi Portal is approximately 
1,88,690 hectare (details annexed at Annexure -A) and compensation 
disbursed is approximately ₹ 53,196 crore. However, title disputes and 
apportionment of compensation between contesting partie s claiming 
compensation is referred to the Principal Civil Court having jurisdiction 
and the assessed compensation amount is deposited in the court.   
  
          Government in Ministry of Road Transport and Highways has 
conducted various capacity building  trainings/ workshops of Central/ 
State officials involved in land acquisition process at Central/ State -
level institutes, State capitals, etc. Remedies such as objections and 
arbitration mechanisms under the NH Act, 1956, Centralized Public 
Grievance Redr ess and Monitoring System (CPGRAMS), etc. are 
available with the landowners for resolution of their grievances. 
  
          The progress of National Highway projects, including land 
acquisition, is regularly monitored by the Government at various 
levels, b y conducting coordination meetings led by the Chief 
Secretaries of States/ UTs where unresolved issues, if any, are 

escalated for further review through the Project Monitoring Group and 
also through “PRAGATI”. 
  
(f)      The State/ UT -wise details of numbe r of National Highway 
projects which are currently under construction, without attaining 
project completion and excluding projects under consideration of 
termination/ foreclosure are annexed at Annexure-B.

3008.  Shri VISHNU DAYAL RAM: 
Shri ANUP SANJAY DHOTRE: 
Shri DAMODAR AGRAWAL: 
Smt. SANJNA JATAV: 
Shri TEJASVI SURYA: 
Smt. SMITA UDAY WAGH:

Shri TRIVENDRA SINGH RAWAT: 
SMT. KAMALJEET SEHRAWAT: 
SHRI GODAM NAGESH: 
Will the Minister of JAL SHAKTI be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has undertaken any revie w of the implementation 
of the National Aquifer Mapping and Management Prog ramme (NAQUIM 2.0) in 

2 
 
the country and if so, the details and the major ou tcomes thereof, State-wise, 
particularly in Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh, Uttara khand, Madhya Pradesh 
including Dewas-Shajapur Lok Sabha Constituency and  Odisha including 
Kandhamal Lok Sabha Constituency; 
(b) the progress achieved in high-resolution aquife r mapping and preparation of 
area-specific groundwater management plans under th e programme in the 
country, State-wise, particularly in Maharashtra in cluding Jalgaon Lok Sabha 
Constituency, district-wise in Andhra Pradesh inclu ding Konaseema district and 
district-wise in Madhya Pradesh including Dewas and Shajapur districts; 
(c) the details of the mechanism established to fac ilitate utilisation of scientific 
inputs generated under NAQUIM 2.0 by various State Governments including the 
State Government of Andhra Pradesh, Panchayati Raj Institutions and local 
bodies for groundwater planning and management; 
(d) the manner in which the said programme is expec ted to strengthen 
evidence-based groundwater management and the steps  taken to promote 
evidence-based sustainable groundwater management, climate-resilient water 
management in the country, particularly in Rajastha n, Andhra Pradesh including 
Konaseema district and Madhya Pradesh including Dew as Shajapur Lok Sabha 
Constituency; 
(e) whether the Government proposes to extend NAQUI M 2.0 interventions to 
groundwater stressed areas in Jalgaon Lok Sabha Con stituency and if so, the 
details thereof; and 
(f) the funds allocated, released and utilised for implementation of NAQUIM 2.0 
in Andhra Pradesh during the last three years? 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR JAL SHAKTI  
(SHRI RAJ BHUSHAN CHOUDHARY) 
(a) to (e) The Central Ground Water Board (CGWB) ha s completed aquifer 
mapping under the National Aquifer Mapping and Mana gement Programme 
(NAQUIM 1.0), covering about 25 lakh sq. km of the identified mappable area of 
the country and has shared aquifer maps and Aquifer  Management Plans with 

3 
 
the concerned State Governments. Building upon this , NAQUIM 2.0 was initiated 
in 2023 for preparation of high-resolution aquifer maps and issue-specific 
groundwater management plans in identified priority  areas such as water-
stressed regions, groundwater quality-affected area s, urban agglomerations, 
industrial clusters, coastal aquifers and springsheds. 
NAQUIM 2.0, approved in 2023, provides for 143 stud ies covering areas  
about 76,857 sq. km across the country during 2023- 24 to 2025-26. These 
studies generate high-resolution scientific informa tion on aquifer 
characteristics, groundwater availability and quali ty, recharge potential and 
groundwater stress, which form the basis for prepar ation of area-specific 
Aquifer Management Plans recommending suitable supp ly-side and demand-side 
interventions. The aquifer maps, groundwater data a nd management plans are 
shared with the concerned State Governments, Distri ct Administrations, 
Panchayati Raj Institutions, Urban Local Bodies and  other stakeholders for 
integration into groundwater recharge, sustainable groundwater development, 
water-resource planning and climate-resilient groun dwater management. CGWB 
also undertakes stakeholder consultations, dissemin ation workshops and 
capacity-building programmes to facilitate effectiv e utilisation of the scientific 
outputs under the programme. The programme facilita tes evidence-based 
groundwater management by providing scientific inpu ts for groundwater 
recharge, sustainable groundwater development, clim ate-resilient water-
resource planning and convergence with various Cent ral and State Government 
programmes. 
The State/area-wise status of NAQUIM 2.0 studies an d the major 
outcomes in respect of Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh,  Uttarakhand, Rajasthan, 
Madhya Pradesh and Odisha, including the districts and Lok Sabha 
Constituencies referred to in the Question are given below: 
i. Maharashtra: NAQUIM 2.0 covers eight identified stu dy areas with an 
aggregate area of about 8,371 sq. km, selected on t he basis of scientific 
prioritisation of water-stressed areas, groundwater  quality-affected areas, 

4 
 
urban agglomerations, industrial clusters, coastal aquifers and 
springsheds. Jalgaon district was covered under NAQ UIM 1.0 and its 
Aquifer Management Plan, published in 2022, recomme nded construction 
of 617 artificial recharge structures with an estim ated recharge potential 
of about 39.64 Million Cubic Metres (MCM) and adopt ion of micro-irrigation 
over about 464.05 sq. km, with an estimated groundw ater saving of about 
156.57 MCM. Jalgaon district is not among the identified study areas under 
NAQUIM 2.0. 
ii. Andhra Pradesh: NAQUIM 2.0 covers five identified s tudy areas with an 
aggregate area of about 3,155 sq. km in selected ur ban agglomerations 
and water-stressed areas. Konaseema district was co vered under NAQUIM 
1.0 over a mappable area of about 2,079.95 sq. km. The Aquifer 
Management Plan delineated five aquifer systems and  recommended 
artificial recharge, conjunctive use of surface wat er and groundwater, 
management of waterlogging and protection of coasta l aquifers. 
Konaseema district is not among the identified stud y areas under NAQUIM 
2.0. 
iii. Uttarakhand: NAQUIM 2.0 covers four identified stud y areas with an 
aggregate area of about 3,567 sq. km for preparatio n of high-resolution 
aquifer maps and area-specific groundwater manageme nt plans. The 
studies generated scientific information on aquifer  characteristics, 
groundwater availability and quality, recharge pote ntial and suitable 
supply-side and demand-side interventions for susta inable groundwater 
management. 
iv. Rajasthan: NAQUIM 2.0 covers five identified study areas with an 
aggregate area of about 1,410 sq. km. Under NAQUIM 1.0, about 3.43 lakh 
sq. km covering the then 33 districts of the State was mapped and the 
aquifer maps and Aquifer Management Plans were shar ed with the State 
Government for evidence-based groundwater planning and management. 

5 
 
v. Madhya Pradesh: NAQUIM 2.0 covers six identified st udy areas with an 
aggregate area of about 3,640 sq. km. Dewas and Sha japur districts were 
covered under NAQUIM 1.0, under which the respectiv e Aquifer 
Management Plans recommended construction of 3,313 artificial recharge 
structures in Dewas district and 856 in Shajapur di strict. The plans also 
recommend demand-side measures such as micro-irriga tion, crop 
diversification and improved water-use efficiency f or sustainable 
groundwater management. Dewas and Shajapur district s are not among 
the identified study areas under NAQUIM 2.0. 
vi. Odisha: NAQUIM 2.0 covers eight identified study ar eas with an aggregate 
area of about 2,990 sq. km in selected coastal, ind ustrial, mining, urban, 
water-stressed and groundwater quality-affected are as. Kandhamal Lok 
Sabha Constituency is not among the identified study areas under NAQUIM 
2.0. 
(f) Under the National Aquifer Mapping and Manageme nt Programme (NAQUIM 
2.0), CGWB undertakes scientific studies for prepar ation of high-resolution 
aquifer maps and area specific Aquifer Management P lans under the Ground 
Water Management and Regulation (GWMR) Scheme, a Ce ntral Sector Scheme. 
Funds under the GWMR Scheme are utilised by CGWB fo r carrying out these 
studies and are not released to the State Governmen ts. Since water is a State 
subject, planning, funding, implementation of water  resources projects, 
including implementation of the recommendations con tained in the Aquifer 
Management Plans are the responsibility of the respective State Governments in 
accordance with their priorities and available reso urces. Accordingly, no funds 
are allocated or released to the State Governments specifically for

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF MICRO, SMALL AND MEDIUM ENTERPRISES 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION No. 3009 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 06.08.2026 
 
IMPLEMENTATION OF PMEGP IN PERAMBALUR 
 
3009.   THIRU ARUN NEHRU: 
 
Will the Minister of MICRO, SMALL AND MEDIUM ENTERPRISES be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  the total financial subsidies and margin money disbursed under the Prime Minister's 
Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP) within the Perambalur Lok Sabha constituency of 
Tamil Nadu over the last three years; 
 
(b)  the specific number of new agro -based and textile manufacturing micro -units successfully 
established by the local youth and women entrepreneurs in the Perambalur district during the said 
period; 
 
(c)  whether the Ministry has noted a high rate of rejection of the applications or excessive demands 
for collateral by the regional rural banks, contrary to the central scheme guidelines and if so, the details 
thereof; 
 
(d)  the total formal employment directly generated by these PMEGP -funded enterprises within the  
said constituency during the last three years; and 
 
(e)  the administrative steps being taken by the Government to simplify the online application 
process and conduct targeted entrepreneurship awareness camps in the rural blocks of Perambalur? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR MICRO, SMALL AND MEDIUM ENTERPRISES 
(SUSHRI SHOBHA KARANDLAJE) 
 
(a): Margin Money (MM) Subsidy amounting to Rs. 5.66 crore has been disbursed under the Prime 
Minister's Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP) in the Perambalur Lok Sabha constituency of 
Tamil Nadu during the last three years i.e. FY 2023-24 to FY 2025-26. 
 
(b): During the last three years, 26 micro‑enterprises have been established under agro‑based 
industries and 1 micro‑enterprise under textile manufacturing by entrepreneurs, including local youth, 
in the Perambalur district. Out of these, 9 micro‑enterprises we re established by women entrepreneurs 
in the agro‑based sector during the said period. 
 
(c): The Ministry has not observed any excessive collateral demands or unusually high rejection 
rates by Regional Rural Banks under PMEGP. As per RBI Master Directions on lending to MSMEs, no 
collateral security is to be insisted by Banks for projects involving loan up to Rs. 20 lakh and strict 
compliance of this provision has been reemphasized to all the financing Banks. On the contrary, 
rejection rates have shown a dec lining trend, reducing from 52% to 46% during the last three years, 
reflecting improved implementation of the scheme in line with scheme guidelines. 

: 2 : 
 
 
 
(d): Sustainable employment opportunities to around 3,105 persons have been generated through 
PMEGP assisted micro enterprises within the Perambalur Lok Sabha constituency during the last three 
years. 
 
(e): Steps taken by the  Government to simplify the online application process and conduct targeted 
entrepreneurship awareness camps under PMEGP throughout the country including rural blocks of 
Perambalur in Tamil Nadu include the following: 
 
i. PMEGP Portal developed as an end -to-end digital platform is integrated with financing banks 
through Jan Samarth Portal, streamlining the approval process with SMS alert to applicants at 
different stages. 
ii. Establishment of PMEGP Helpdesks at State Offices to provide real-time assistance and hand-
holding support to potential beneficiaries. 
iii. A wide range of more than 1,000 Model of Detailed Project Reports prepared on various 
industries has been made available on the PMEGP portal. 
iv. Awareness and outreach programmes in all the States/UTs including bac kward and under -
performing areas, Aspirational districts, NER etc. to identify potential beneficiaries and 
provide handholding support during the application process.

 Will the Minister of POWER 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether the Government proposes to implement any special scheme for the 
modernisation of sub-stations and transmission network to address the issues of 
frequent power tripping and low voltage in Etawah Lok Sabha Constituency; and 
 
(b)  if so, the details thereof? 
 
A N S W E R 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF POWER  
 
(SHRI SHRIPAD NAIK)  
 
(a) & (b):       As reported by the Uttar Pradesh Power Transmission Corporation 
Ltd (UPPTCL), there is no issues of frequent power tripping or low volt age

Will the Minister of TRIBAL AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
  
(a) whether the Government had issued a letter on 5 June 2025 directing the State Government 
of Uttarakhand and the district administrations to expedite the recognition of the rights of Van 
Gujjars over seasonal grazing areas in response to the harassment faced by them during their 
seasonal migration, if so, the details thereof; 
  
(b) the action taken by the Tribal Department of the State Government of Uttarakhand in

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3013 
TO BE ANSWERED ON AUGUST 06, 2026 
 
 
SLUM REHABILITATION SCHEME 
 
 
 
NO. 3013  DR. ALOK KUMAR SUMAN:   
 
Will the Minister of HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) the present status of slum rehabilitation schemes in the country; 
(b) the steps taken by the Government to provide affordable housing in 
urban areas; 
(c) the progress made under housing schemes for the urban poor; 
(d) the present status of the land allocation policy for housing projects; 
and 
(e) the manner in which housing development is being undertaken under 
the Smart Cities Mission? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE  
MINISTRY OF HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS 
(SHRI TOKHAN SAHU) 
 
(a) to ( d): ‘Land’ and ‘Colonisation’ are State subjects. Therefore, 
schemes related to housing, slum rehabilitation and land allocation for 
housing projects  for their citizens are implemented by States/Union 
Territories (UTs) in their respective areas. However, Ministry of Housing 
and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) supplements the efforts of States/UTs by 
providing Central Assistance under Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana – Urban 
(PMAY-U) since June 25, 2015 to provide pucca houses to all eligible 
urban beneficiaries including urban homeless and slum dwellers across 
the country. 
 
Based on the learnings from the experiences of implementation of PMAY-
U, MoHUA has revamped the scheme and launched PMAY-U 2.0 ‘Housing 
for All’ Mission with effect from 01.09.2024 for implementation in urban 
areas across the country to support 1 crore additional eligible 
beneficiaries. PMAY-U 2.0 is implemented through four verticals i.e., 
Beneficiary Led Construction (BLC), Affordable Housing in Partnership  
…2/- 

-2- 
(AHP), Affordable Rental Housing (ARH) and Interest Subsidy Scheme 
(ISS). The Scheme Guidelines can be accessed at https://pmay -
urban.gov.in/uploads/guidelines/Operational-Guidelines-of-PMAY-U-2.pdf. 
 
Based on the project proposal submitted by States/Union Territories 
(UTs), a total of 127.68 lakh houses including 16.20 lakh under PMAY -U 
2.0 have been sanctioned by the Ministry including slums in cities across 
the country as 13.07.2026. Out of which, 121.03 lakh houses have been 
grounded, 99.07 lakh are completed of which 96.73 lakh are occupied 
across the country as on 13.07.2026 under PMAY-U & PMAY-U 2.0. A total 
of ₹2.12 lakh crores of Central Assistance has been approved of which 
₹1.81 lakh crore have been released to States/UTs based on the 
compliances submitted by them.  Out of total houses sanctioned under 
the scheme, more than  29 lakh houses have been sanctioned to slum 
dwellers.   
 
(e): The Smart Cities Mission (SCM) adopted an integrated approach to 
urban development, wherein housing was as part of comprehensive city 
planning rather than as a standalone component. Since the SCM period 
is over on 31.03.2025, no new schemes are being undertaken now.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
  
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. - 3014 
ANSWERED ON 06th AUGUST, 2026 
  
SCHEMES FOR ROAD ACCIDENT VICTIMS 
  
3014. SHRI ARUN KUMAR SAGAR: 
   
Will the Minister of ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS  
  
सड़क परिवहन औि िाजमार्ग मंत्री 
be pleased to state: 
  
(a) the details of the Central schemes for road accident victims in the 
country; 
(b) the details of the compensation and medical assistance provided 
under these schemes; 
(c) the  number of road accident victims benefited under these 
schemes in the Shahjahanpur Parliamentary Constituency; 
(d) the details of the issues being faced in the disbursement of 
compensation to such victims in the country; and 
(e) the impact of these schemes  on providing assistance to road 
accident victims? 
ANSWER 
  
THE MINISTER OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
                                                                                         
(SHRI NITIN JAIRAM GADKARI) 
(a) and (b) The Central Government has put in place the following 
schemes for providing emergency medical care through cashless 

treatment of road accident victims and compensation to victims of hit 
& run motor accidents: 
(i) Prime Minister Road Accident Victims’ Hospitalisation and Assured 
Treatment (PM -RAHAT) Scheme:  Introduced in accordance with the 
legal mandate under Section 162 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the 
Cashless Treatment of Road Acccident Victims scheme provides 
treatment cover upto ₹1.5 lakh per victim, subject to a maximum  cap 
of 7 days from the date of accident on any category of road. Further, 
the treatment cover will be available to all those victims who are 
involved in road accidents caused by use of motor vehicles. 
(ii) Compensation to Victims of Hit and Run Motor Acci dents Scheme, 
2022: As per Section 161 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the Central 
Government is required to provide compensation in respect of death or 
grievous hurt resulting from hit -and-run motor accidents. Accordingly, 
the Compensation to Victims of Hit and Run Motor Accidents Scheme, 
2022 was notified vide G.S.R. 163(E) and is being implemented with 
effect from 01.04.2022. Under the Scheme, a fixed compensation of 
Rs. 2 lakh is provided in case of death and Rs. 50,000 in case of 
grievous hurt.  
(c) As on 31.07.2026, the following is the status of beneficiaries in the 
Shahjahanpur Parliamentary Constituency: 
Under the PM -RAHAT Scheme, 1 road accident victim has been 
registered for treatment. The corresponding eDAR request was 
approved by the police, ma king the victim eligible for full treatment 
coverage in accordance with the Scheme provisions. 
Under the Compensation to Victims of Hit and Run Motor Accidents 
Scheme, 2022, 2 claims have been received and settled.  
(d) Time -bound procedures and clearly de fined responsibilities have 
been prescribed under the respective Schemes to minimise delays in 
the provision of treatment, processing of claims and disbursement of 
compensation: 
Under the PM -RAHAT Scheme, treatment is initiated upon admission 
and police authentication is undertaken in parallel through the 

integrated Transaction Management System (TMS) portal of National 
Health Authority (NHA) and Electronic Detailed Accident Repor t 
(eDAR) portal. After discharge, the hospital submits its claim to the 
State Health Agency for verification and approval. To ensure timely 
payments to the hospitals, a period of 10 days has been defined from 
the claim being approved by SHA for District Co llectors or GI council 
to make the payments, as the case maybe. Beyond the prescribed 
time, the claim shall be deemed approved. The end -to-end digital 
workflow provides a complete trail from accident reporting and 
treatment to claim approval and final payment. 
Similarly, the Compensation to Victims of Hit and Run Motor Accidents 
Scheme, 2022 provides a time -bound process for settlement of claims. 
The Claims Enquiry Officer is required to submit the enquiry report 
within one month of receipt of the applicati on, the Claims Settlement 
Commissioner is required to sanction the claim within 15 days of 
receiving the report, and the General Insurance Council (GIC) is 
required to transfer the compensation to the claimant within a further 
period of 15 days. 
  
(e) The PM-RAHAT Scheme is formulated to achieve the objective of 
reducing fatalities and provide financial certainty to the hospitals 
ensuring non-denial of treatment to road accident victims. Integration 
of Emergency Response Support System (ERSS - 112), acciden t 
reporting mechanism for police (eDAR) and the designated hospital 
network (TMS 2.0) facilitates ambulance support, identification of the 
nearest designated hospital, prompt initiation of treatment, parallel 
police authentication and direct reimbursement to hospitals. 
The Compensation to Victims of Hit and Run Motor Accidents Scheme, 
2022 provides fixed financial assistance of Rs. 2 lakh in case of death 
and Rs. 50,000 in case of grievous hurt, where the offending vehicle 
cannot be identified. The prescrib ed time-bound claims process, along 
with digital processing, eDAR linkage and monitoring through the 
District Road Safety Committees and State Road Safety Councils, 
supports transparent and timely disbursement to eligible claimants. 

The Government has inst ituted the Rah -Veer Scheme to encourage 
citizens to assist victims of serious road accidents during the Golden 
Hour. The Scheme operates along with the protections provided to 
Good Samaritans under Section 134A of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 
and the Good Samaritan Rules notified vide G.S.R. 594(E) dated 
29.09.2020. Any individual who has assisted a victim of a serious 
accident involving a motor vehicle by administering immediate 
assistance and rushing the victim to a Hospital/Trauma Care Centre 
within the Golden Hour of the accident for medical treatment is 
eligible for a cash reward of Rs. 25,000 per incident, along with a 
Certificate of Appreciation, subject to the provisions of the Scheme.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3015 
ANSWERED ON 06TH AUGUST 2026 
 
EXPRESSION OF INTEREST FOR APC SCHEME 
  
3015. ADV GOWAAL KAGADA PADAVI: 
             
Will the Minister of FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES be pleased to state: 
    
(a) the number of Expression of Interest (EoIs) received for Agro Processing Clusters (APC) 
Scheme in Maharashtra post-2020 and project approved, district-wise; 
(b) the status of the twelve Maharashtra APC projects including original timelines, current physical 
progress, revised completion timelines with penalties, if any, imposed on execution agencies; 
(c) the grant utilization percentage and specific reasons for prolonged “Under Implementation” 
status for the same; and 
(d) the concrete steps taken to provide market access and reduce post-harvest losses via. Pradhan 
Mantri Kisan Sampada Yojana (PMKSY) and Production Linked Incentive Scheme for Food 
Processing Industries (PLISFPI), including number of beneficiaries and value addition units 
established thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES 
(SHRI CHIRAG PASWAN) 
  
(a): The Ministry of Food Processing Industries (MoFPI) has been implementing the Scheme for 
Creation of Infrastructure for Agro Processing Clusters (APC) since 2017 as a component scheme of 
the Pradhan Mantri Kisan Sampada Yojana (PMKSY). Proposals under the APC Scheme are invited 
from prospective investors / entrepreneurs through Expressions of Interest (EoIs) issued by MoFPI 
from time to time. The district-wise details of EoIs received for APCs in Maharashtra post-2020 and 
projects approved are at Annexure-I. 
  
(b) to (c):  The status of twelve approved projects under APC Scheme in the State of Maharashtra, 
including original timelines, current physical progress and grant utilization percentage is at Annexure-
II. The Ministry considers and accords extensions in timelines under the Scheme Guidelines. Further, 
the delay in implementing the projects is mainly due to project-specific issues such as delay in 
obtaining statutory clearances, including planning implementation, land acquisition, regulatory 
clearances, market linkages and technology adoption and penalty, wherever applicable, is imposed on 
the Project Implementing Agency for delay in completion of the project, in accordance with the 
provisions of the Scheme Guidelines. 
 
(d): The component schemes under PMKSY provide financial assistance in the form of grants-in-
aid/subsidy. The scheme is aimed at creating modern food processing infrastructure and value addition 
facilities, strengthening the food processing sector, reducing post-harvest losses, enhancing the 
processing and preservation of agricultural produce, generating employment, and providing better 
remuneration to farmers. 

  
As of 30.06.2026, under PMKSY, 1735 projects have been approved (1,256 
completed/operational), benefiting 37.76 lakh farmers, generating 9.16 lakh jobs, and creating 294.21 
LMT per annum of processing/preservation capacity.  
  
PLISFPI provides performance-linked incentives on incremental sales to promote domestic 
processing, value addition, capacity expansion, and modernization. Its Branding & Marketing Abroad 
component grants 50% of eligible expenditure, capped at 3% of sales or ₹50 crore annually, whichever 
is less. 
  
Under PLISFPI, in Maharashtra, 41 manufacturing units are operational and Rs.1368.71 crore have 
been invested. Approved PLI units, manufacturing products across segments including RTC/RTE 
foods, processed fruits & vegetables, marine products, mozzarella cheese, millet-based items, and 
innovative/organic foods, have added approximately 4,33,982 MT per annum of processing capacity.

TO BE ANSWERED ON 06th August, 2026 
 
LPG Distribution in Tamil Nadu 
 
3017. Shri Mani A: 
 
पेĚोͧलयम एवं Ĥाकृ Ǔतक गैस मंğी 
 
 Will the Minister of PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has undertaken measures to strengthen the Liquefied Petroleum 
Gas (LPG) distribution network in Tamil Nadu, particularly in Dharmapuri Parliamentary 
Constituency, to ensure timely and convenient access to domestic LPG for all households, if 
so, the details thereof; 
 
(b) the number of LPG distributors, delivery points and LPG consumers in Dharmapuri 
Parliamentary Constituency and the steps taken to expand the distribution infrastructure 
during the last three years; 
 
(c) whether the Government proposes to establish additional LPG distributorships or 
strengthen delivery logistics in rural and remote areas of Dharmapuri to improve last-mile 
service delivery, if so, the details thereof; and 
 
(d) the measures taken to promote consumer safety, digital booking, doorstep delivery and 
timely refill supply and to further enhance LPG accessibility and service quality across Tamil 
Nadu including Dharmapuri Parliamentary Constituency? 
 
ANSWER 
 
पेĚोͧलयम एवं Ĥाकृ Ǔतक गैस मंğालय मɅ राÏयमंğी 
(Įी सुरेश गोपी) 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS 
(SHRI SURESH GOPI) 
 
(a) to (d): Appointment of LPG distributorships by the Public Sector Oil Marketing 
Companies (OMCs) is a continuous process and locations for setting up of LPG 
distributorships are identified and advertised under Unified Selection Guidelines 2016.  
As on 01.07.2026, there are a total of 25,611 LPG distributorships of PSU OMCs across the 
country, including 1658 in state of Tamil Nadu, out of which 17,685 distributorships are 
serving rural areas. These are served through 214 LPG bottling plants of Oil Marketing 
Companies (OMCs) located across the country. In order to improve access of LPG in rural 
and remote areas, PSU OMCs have commissioned 8045 distributorships, during 01.04.2016 
to 30.06.2026 across the country, out of which 7452 (i.e. 93 %) are catering to rural areas.  
All distributors, except Durgam Kshetriya Vitraks, are mandated to make home delivery of 
LPG cylinders in their area of operation. 

Dharmapuri Parliamentary Constituency covers Dharmapuri and Salem districts and is served 
by a total of 110 LPG distributors of Public Sector Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs), out of 
which 02 LPG distributorship have been commissioned during last 3 Financial Years. As on 
01.07.2026, there were about total 15.80 lakh domestic LPG consumers in these two districts.  
To further improve last-mile delivery in remote and underserved habitations, OMCs have 
taken several measures, including commissioning of rural and remote-area distributorships, 
appointment of Common Service Center - Village Level Entrepreneur (CSC VLEs), etc. 
OMCs have 162 numbers of CSC VLEs in these aforesaid 02 districts to ensure the last mile 
availability of LPG.   
To ensure the timely availability of LPG refills, all domestic LPG consumers can book a refill 
by various methods including Interactive Voice Response System(IVRS), Short Message 
Service(SMS), Whatsapp, calling directly on the phone of distributor, e-commerce platforms, 
OMC mobile applications, OMCs web-portals etc. These different options provide enhanced 
user accessibility for seamless and hassle-free booking of LPG refills. 
 
The average refill delivery time in Tamil Nadu is 1.6 days as of 01.08.2026. 
 
To improve awareness amongst LPG consumers, a Basic Safety campaign was organised 
during 2024-2025 across the country under the theme “Khushiyan Ab Teen Guna” with the 
objective of reaching the doorsteps of domestic LPG customers. The campaign was designed 
to educate consumers on the safe usage of LPG, complemented by extensive mass awareness 
initiatives through print and electronic media, on-site safety checks at customer premises, and 
the replacement of Suraksha hoses. The campaign achieved significant progress with over 
12.12 crore free basic safety checks conducted at customer premises without any cost to 
consumer including 82.42 lakh in state of Tamil Nadu and more than 4.65 crore LPG hoses 
replaced at discounted rates including 41 lakh in state of Tamil Nadu.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF JAL SHAKTI 
DEPARTMENT OF DRINKING WATER & SANITATION 
  
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3018 
ANSWERED ON 06/08/2026 
EXTENSION OF JAL JEEVAN MISSION 
 
3018.   SHRI NARESH GANPAT MHASKE: 
SMT. BHARTI PARDHI: 
DR. SHRIKANT EKNATH SHINDE: 
DR. RAJ KUMAR CHABBEWAL: 
SHRI SHRIRANG APPA CHANDU BARNE: 
SHRI RAVINDRA DATTARAM WAIKAR: 
 
Will the Minister of Jal Shakti be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government proposes to extend the Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) up to December 2028 
with the objective of achieving universal coverage of Functional Household Tap Connections 
(FHTCs) across the country and if so, the details thereof; 
(b) the extent of progress achieved un der the said Mission so far including the coverage of rural 
households and improvements made in drinking water infrastructure; 
(c) the reasons and policy considerations that necessitated the proposed extension of the said Mission 
beyond its earlier timeline; 
(d) the strategies being adopted during the extended period to address regional disparities, water 
quality challenges and sustainability of drinking water sources; and 
(e) whether the proposed extension is aligned with the long -term objectives of water security and 
improved public health outcomes and if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR JAL SHAKTI 
(SHRI V. SOMANNA) 
 
(a) & (b) Drinking Water being a State subject, it is the States, who plan, design, approve and 
implement drinking water supply schemes including those under Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM). 
Government of India supplements the efforts of the States by providing technical and financial 
assistance for the implementation of the mission 
In August, 2019, Government of India approv ed Jal Jeevan Mission to be implemented in partnership 
with States for a period of five years (2019-24) for making provision of tap water supply to every rural 
household.  

Page 2 of 2 
 
At the time of announcement of the JJM, only 3.23 crore (17%) rural households were reported to 
have tap water connections in the country. So far, as reported by States/ UTs as on 18.07.2026, around 
12.66 crore additional rural households have been provided with tap water connections. Thus, as on 
18.07.2026, out of 19.36 crore rural house holds in the country, around 15.89 crore (82.09%) 
households are reported to have tap water connections in their homes. 
(c) to (e) To complete the ongoing works, Hon'ble Finance Minister during her budget speech 2025-26 
announced extension of JJM until 2028. In March, 2026, Union Cabinet has approved extension of the 
JJM period up to December 2028, with an enhanced outlay and a restructured implementation 
framework focusing on structural reforms in the rural drinking water supply sector under JJM 2.0. The 
total outlay of the mission has been increased from Rs 3.60 lakh crore to Rs. 8.69 lakh crore with 
enhancement of total central assistance from Rs 2.08 lakh crore to Rs 3.59 lakh crore.  
JJM has been envisioned and implemented as a decentralized, demand -driven and community 
managed programme, wherein the Gram Panchayat (GP) and/ or its sub -committee/ user group i.e. 
Village Water & Sanitation Committee (VWSC)/ Pani Samiti have been empowered to plan, 
implement, manage, operate and maintain in -village water s upply system to provide regular and 
assured tap water supply in rural households. Further, provision has been made in the operational 
guidelines for implementation of JJM for the preparation of Village Action Plan (VAP) for engaging 
village community, which inter alia includes strengthening of drinking water sources in convergence 
with other schemes. 
To promote Jan Bhagidari for sustainable and continuous service delivery under the JJM, a 
standardized “Handbook on Community -Managed Piped Water Systems” has been launched under 
the Jal Arpan initiative. The handbook mandates a 15 -day trial run involving GPs and VWSC/ Pani 
Samiti members to ensure smooth handover of water supply schemes and sustainable operations. In 
addition, Jal Seva Ankalan has been initiate d as a Gram Panchayat led digital assessment tool for 
evaluating the functionality and service delivery of rural drinking water supply systems. 
Moreover, for enabling the local village community to play their role in operation and maintenance of 
water supply schemes, Nal Jal Mitra Programme (NJMP) has been launched in collaboration with 
Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship to equip them with a comprehensive set of skills 
& develop “Nal Jal Mitras”, so that they can function as scheme operators  and are able to carry out 
minor repairs and maintenance, including preventive maintenance, of the piped water supply 
scheme(s) in their village as skilled masons, plumbers, fitters, electricians, motor mechanics, pump 
operators, etc. 
Provisions have also been made for planning and implementation of bulk water transfer from long 
distances and regional water supply schemes for ensuring tap water supply in drought -prone & water-
scarce areas/ areas with inadequate rainfall or dependable ground water sources. I n addition, 
provisions have been made for source recharging, viz. dedicated bore well recharge structures, rain 
water recharge, rejuvenation of existing water bodies, etc., in convergence with other schemes such as 
VB-G RAM G, Integrated Watershed Manageme nt Programme (IWMP), 15th and 16th Finance 
Commission tied grants to RLBs/ PRIs, State schemes, CSR funds, etc. 
JJM 2.0 also fosters the vision of Viksit Bharat @ 2047 with assured supply of drinking water by 
shifting from infrastructure -centric approach t o a citizen -centric utility -based service delivery 
approach through Structural Reforms.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF POWER 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO.3019 
ANSWERED ON 06.08.2026 
 
REPLACEMENT OF FAULTY DISTRIBUTION TRANSFORMERS 
 
†3019. SHRI BHARAT SINGH KUSHWAH: 
 
 Will the Minister of POWER 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether inordinate delays in t he replacement of faulty Distribution 
Transformers in rural and semi-urban areas are resulting in prolonged disruption 
of electricity supply and if so, the details thereof;  
 
(b)  whether overloading of Distribution Transformers, pending pole shifting at 
various locations and dilapidated electricity poles situated in densely populated 
areas are increasing the risk of accidents and if so, the details thereof;  
 
(c)  whether the Government is preparing any time -bound national action plan 
to ensure decentralis ation of Distribution Transformers, expeditious shifting of 
dilapidated electricity poles and poles located in densely populated areas, 
installation of underground/cable-based electricity lines and early electrification 
of long-inhabited majras, tolas, new colonies and settlements in coordination with 
the States; and  
 
(d)  if so, the details thereof? 
A N S W E R 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF POWER  
 
(SHRI SHRIPAD NAIK)  
 
(a) to (d) : Electricity is a concurrent subject and power distribution is handled by 
distribution utilities that function under the guidance of their respective State 
Electricity Regulatory Commission (SERC) and State Government. As per the 
Electricity Act, 2003, distribution of electricity is a licensed activity and it is the 
duty of the respective distribution licensee to develop and maintain an efficient 
and safe distribution system in its area of supply. Hence, the responsibility for 
taking necessary measures for the upgradation and maintenance of the 
distribution system and regularly checking the structural strength of poles and 
wires of High Tension (HT) and Low Tension (LT) lines to ensure quality and 
reliable power supply and necessary safety measures, rests with the respective 
distribution utilities, including taking action on complaints in this regard. 
 
………2. 

 
- 2 - 
 
CEA (Measures relating to Safety and Electric Supply) Regulations, 2023, 
specify safety measures for construction, operation and maintenance of power 
stations, sub-stations, transmission and distribution lines. These regulations lay 
down the safety measures for electrical installations and provide for periodic 
inspection and testing of electrical installations. In addition, the CEA (Technical 
Standards for Construction of Electrical Plants and Electric Lines) Regulations, 
2022, contain specific provisions for strengthening of poles and wires in disaster 
prone areas and coastal areas to withstand severe environmental stress. The 
above regulations are applicable to all entities who generate, transmit or 
distribute electricity. 
 
Government of India (GoI) has supplemented the efforts of the States to 
help them provide quality supply of power earlier through schemes like Deen 
Dayal Upadhyaya Gram Jyoti Yojana (DDUGJY) launched in 2014, Pradhan Mantri 
Sahaj Bijli Har Ghar Yojana (SAUBHAGYA) launched in October 2017, and 
currently under the Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (RDSS) launched in 
July 2021. 
 
Under RDSS, financial assistance is being provided to Distribution Utilities 
for upgradation of distribution infras tructure works such as 
upgradation/augmentation of substations and distribution transformers, 
replacement of conductors, new HT/LT lines, feeder bifurcation, feeder 
segregation, Aerial Bunched Cables (ABC)/covered conductors, underground 
cables and smart m etering, based on proposals submitted by the Distribution 
Utilities. Under the scheme, loss reduction infrastructure works amounting to Rs. 
1.53 lakh crore and smart metering works amounting to Rs. 1.31 lakh crore have 
been sanctioned at the national level.  
 
Government of India is further supporting the States for grid electrification 
of left -out households under RDSS. Under RDSS, on -grid electrification works 
amounting to Rs. 6,521 crore have been sanctioned for electrification of 13.65 
lakh left -out hous eholds, wherever found feasible, including households 
belonging to Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs) identified under 
Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan (PM -JANMAN); Scheduled 
Tribes (STs) under Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh  Abhiyan (DA -JGUA); 
Scheduled Castes (SCs) under Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana 
(PM-AJAY); and households in remote and border areas under the Vibrant Village 
Programme (VVP), wherever found feasible. As on 23.07.2026, 4.88 lakh 
households have been electrified under RDSS and state schemes.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3021 
ANSWERED ON 06TH AUGUST, 2026 
 
MAINTENANCE OF HIGHWAY SANITATION 
3021.   SHRI AZAD KIRTI JHA: 
       
Will the Minister of ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
 
सड़क परिवहन औि िाजमार्ग मंत्री 
be pleased to state: 
(a) the steps taken by the Government to ensure sustained 
maintenance of highway sanitation  beyond campaign periods to 
prevent relapse into unsanitary conditions; 
(b) the details of provisions in place for incentivizing or penalizing  
concessionaires under  performance-based contracts for highway 
cleanliness and upkeep; 
(c) the percentage of ongoing and completed National Highway  
projects that have  incorporated eco -friendly construction materials 
and energy -efficient street lighting systems along  with the details of 
such projects; 
(d) the mechanisms in place for independent verification of 
compliance and the steps being  taken to expand designated green 
corridors; and 
(e) whether the Government has initiated or proposed pilot projects 
employing Internet of Things (IoT), Artificial Intelligence (AI) and other 
emerging technologies for smart highway  operations and enhanced 
traffic management and if so, the details thereof? 
 
  

ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
 
(SHRI NITIN JAIRAM GADKARI) 
(a) Government in Ministry of Road Transport and Highways is 
primarily responsible for development and maintenance of National 
Highways (NHs). Apart from organising cleanliness drives / campaigns 
on NHs, Government  has undertaken various initiatives to ensure the 
sustained maintenance of highway sanitation on NHs, some of which 
are as under: - 
i. Strict contractual maintenance obligations and penalty clauses 
incorporated in Operation & Maintenance (O&M) and concession 
/ contract agreements, making Contractors / Concessionaires 
directly accountable for maintenance of project highway, 
roadside drains, culverts, medians, slopes, structures, and Right 
of Way (RoW) in a clean and hygienic condition by regularly 
removing debr is, litter, waste materials, hazardous spillages, 
organic growth etc. 
ii. Routine inspection by Authority Engineer (AE) / Independent 
Engineer (IE) to monitor compliance with maintenance 
obligations and ensure highway amenities, user fee plazas and 
wayside rest stops maintain hygiene standards year-round.   
iii. Deployment of dedicated maintenance mobile application / 
dashboard to report, track and resolve sanitation issues in real 
time. 
iv. Directions issued for construction of toilet facilities at all NH 
User Fee Plazas in both directions after crossing the plaza where 
such facilities are not presently available; temporary pre -
fabricated or mobile toilet blocks to be placed on newly 
completed access -controlled NHs till Wayside Amenities come 
up. 

v. Mapping of toilet facil ities on the Rajmarg Yatra App as well as 
installation of advance signages for public visibility  for improved 
user experience. 
(b) Government has adopted structured maintenance mechanisms 
through Performance -Based Maintenance Contracts (PBMC), wherein 
the payment for the deliverables is linked to the Contractor 
successfully meeting certain clearly defined performance indicators / 
Service Levels as defined in the standard PBMC Document. Further, 
there is a provision for penalty / reduction in routine mainten ance 
monthly payment for non -achievement of the desired service levels of 
highway cleanliness and upkeep. 
(c) Government has taken various policy reforms and initiatives to 
promote sustainable development through use of eco -friendly 
construction materials and energy-efficient street lighting systems on 
NHs. Various sustainable and recycled materials, such as use of 
Bamboo Crash Barrier, use of Fly Ash / Pond Ash in embankment and 
structural works, Reclaimed Asphalt Pavement (RAP) in bituminous 
layers, and C onstruction and Demolition (C&D) Waste / Recycled 
Aggregates are used in suitable highway works as per technical 
specifications. The use of plastic waste in bituminous mixes, natural 
geo-textiles (such as Jute/ Coir etc.) in addition to other sustainable 
materials including Slag, Bio Bitumen / Molasses, Crumb Rubber and 
other recycled or industrial by-products are promoted as per feasibility 
and guidelines to improve pavement performance for addressing 
environmental concerns. 
Accordingly, Government has com pleted NHs works in about 
9,400 km using eco -friendly construction materials and NHs works in 
another 5,200 km are under construction. 
Government has also installed solar -based street lighting 
systems in about 3,300 km NH length and installation in another  700 
km has been taken up. 
(d)     As part of the Green Highways (Plantation, Transplantation, 
Beautification and Maintenance) Policy 2015, Government undertakes 

plantation along available surplus median and roadside land of Right 
of Way (ROW) of various N H stretches in the country either as part of 
NHs projects or on standalone basis, in accordance with Indian Roads 
Congress (IRC):SP:21 guidelines. During the last five years, 
approximately 1.32 Lakh km of NHs in the country have been covered 
with the plantation of over 3.61 Crore saplings. 
Miyawaki plantation and drone monitoring of plantation has also 
been started to increase the green cover along NHs apart from 
deployment of External Professionals for implementation and 
supervision of greening endeavors a nd monitoring and evaluation of 
plantations through routine inspection by AE/IE.   
Further, Government has developed the Green Cover Index, 
which uses high -resolution satellite data to assess plantation 
presence and health within NH RoW. The first assessme nt covered 
about 31,000 km across 24 States, with results available on 
Geographic Information System (GIS) based portal hosted on Bhuvan 
geo-platform of Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO). 
(e) Government has been progressively adopting Artificial 
Intelligence (AI), Internet of Things (IoT) and other emerging 
technologies for smart highway operations and enhanced traffic 
management on NHs.  
The Government has envisaged deployment of Advanced Traffic 
Management Systems (ATMS) with the objective of impr oving road 
safety and reducing accidents on NHs. ATMS has provisions for 
various electronic enforcement devices which help in speedy 
identification of incidents (including traffic violations) on the highway 
stretches and effectively monitor the highways, t hereby improving 
incident response time and road safety. The Government has taken up 
Region-wise implementation of ATMS in all Four lane and above NHs in 
a phased manner to have an all -integrated development of traffic 
management rather than project level implementation. Accordingly, 
Government has approved ATMS implementation in 531 km length and 
process has been initiated for approval in another 6,000 km.  

Government has also decided to implement Multi -Lane Free Flow 
(MLFF) Electronic Toll Collection syst em on NHs, which facilitates 
barrier-less tolling using integrated technologies including Automatic 
Number Plate Recognition (ANPR) with AI analytics and RFID -based 
Electronic Toll Collection (FASTag), where the user fee shall be 
charged from the vehicle u sers without having to stop, slow down or 
stay in a given fee plaza lane. 17 fee plazas have been awarded, out of 
which 6 fee plazas are already live.

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE 
MINISTRY OF HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS 
(SHRI TOKHAN SAHU) 
 
(a) and (b): Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation 2.0 
(AMRUT 2.0) was launched on 01 October 2021 in all Urban Local 
Bodies (ULBs)/ cities, enabling the cities to become 'self -reliant' and 
'water secure'. Providing universal coverage of sewerage and septage  
…3/- 

-3- 
management in 500 AMRUT cities is one of the major focus areas of 
AMRUT 2.0. Rejuvenation of water bodies, development of green 
spaces and parks are other components of the Mission.  
 
Under AMRUT 2.0, States/ Union Territories (UTs) are empowered to 
select, appraise, prioritise and implement the projects within the 
broad framework of Mission guidelines. Under AMRUT 2.0, the State 
Water Action Plans (SWAPs) comprising of 8,777  projects with total 
cost of ₹1,97,191.85 crore (including operation and maintenance cost) 
including Central share of ₹66, 638.59 crore have been approved. The 
project includes 3572 water supply projects with approved cost of 
₹1,18,968.38 crore, 605 sewerage and septage management projects 
with approved cost of ₹71,133.01 crore, 2951 water body rejuvenation 
projects with approved cost of ₹ 6003.34 crore and 1649 park projects 
with approved cost of ₹1087.12 crore.  
 
  As reported by the States/ UTs on AMRUT 2.0 portal as on 09.07.2026, 
7,687 projects worth ₹1, 37,130.13 crore (capex cost) have been 
awarded and total works worth ₹66,4 72 crore have been physically 
completed. The status of projects , State/UT and city /ULB-wise 
including ULBs under Nabarangpur Lok Sabha Constituency of Odisha 
and Jalgaon Lok Sabha Constituency of Maharashtra are available on 
the website https://amrut.mohua.gov.in/approvedProjects/state. 
 
 The progress of the Mission is reviewed at various levels in the Ministry 
with the States/ UTs through physical meetings/ video conferences , 
etc. For assessment and monitoring of work done under AMRUT 2.0 in 
the States/UTs, Independent Review and Monitoring Agencies (IRMAs) 
have been engaged by the MoHUA, which periodically review and 
monitor the grounded projects in the States/UTs . The IRMA s give  
project specific observations, which are communicated to the State 
for rectification. The action taken by the State is further reviewed by 
the IRMA. 
 
  (c): Under AMRUT 2.0, funds are released to the States/ UTs and not 
city-wise. States/UTs further release funds to the ULBs/ Implementing 
Agencies as per progress of the projects. Central share of ₹17834.22 
crore has been released/ Sanctioned to the States/ UTs for the projects 
under AMRUT 2.0 in the last three financial years (2023-24 to 2025-26) 
and current year (2026- 27) till 09.07.2026 of which an amount of 
₹14,497.69 crore has been utilised/ expenditure incurred by the States/ 
UTs. State/UT-wise details are given in Annexure.  
…4/- 
 
 
 

-4- 
  (d): The progress of the Mission in the S tates/ UTs including slow 
performing States/ UTs and ULBs is reviewed in the Ministry 
periodically. The Ministry also conducts capacity building programmes 
for ULB officials/ contractors, etc from time to time. The Mission 
guidelines also provide for engage ment of Project Development and 
Management Consultant (PDMC) by the States for planning, design, 
supervision and management of projects. Expenditure on PDMC is fully 
funded by the Centre within the overall allocation of the State under

  (e): As updated by the States/ UTs on AMRUT 2.0 portal as on

ULB/ City -wise water tap connections and sewer connections are

(f): Under AMRUT 2.0, States/ UTs are empowered to select, appraise, 
prioritise and implement the projects within broad framework of 
Mission guidelines. The approved projects, State/UT and city/ULB-wise 
including ULBs under Nabarangpur Lok Sabha Constituency of Odisha 
and Jalgaon Lok Sabha Constituency of Maharashtra are available on 
the website https://amrut.mohua.gov.in/approvedProjects/state.  
 
  (g): As updated by the States/ UTs on the AMRUT 2.0 portal, t he 
approved water supply projects under AMRUT 2.0 includes 
development of a total of 11,769.08 MLD water treatment plant 
capacity, 1. 61 lakh km of water network and around 181 lakh new 
household water tap connections. The sewerage and septage 
management projects include development of a total of 7098.27 MLD 
of Sewerage Treatment Plant capacity, 40,021.24 km of sewer network 
and around 69.41 lakh new household sewer connections. The projects 
under AMRUT 2.0 are infrastructure projects which benefit all the 
people living in the area.  
 
  (h): The Mission guidelines has provision of the State High Powered 
Steering Committee (SHPSC) headed by the Chief Secretary of the 
State to monitor and supervise implementation of the scheme at the 
State/ UT level for their timely completion. Further, an Apex Committee 
constituted under the Mission,  reviews and monitor the Mission

through regular video conferences/ webinars/ workshops/ site- visits 
etc. by Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) with the States/ 
UTs. There i s a dedicated AMRUT  online portal for tracking the

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF JAL SHAKTI 
DEPARTMENT OF WATER RESOURCES, RIVER DEVELOPMENT & GANGA

LOK SABHA
