GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF POWER 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO.3209 
ANSWERED ON 06.08.2026 
 
PROJECTS TO INCREASE POWER GENERATION, TRANSMISSION AND 
DISTRIBUTION CAPACITY 
 
†3209. SHRI RAJESH RANJAN: 
 
 Will the Minister of POWER 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government is implementing any new action plan to increase 
power generation, transmission and distribution capacity in the country by the 
year 2030, if so, the details thereof;  
 
(b) the details of the projects sanctioned for the development of power 
generation, transmission and distribution infrastructure in Bihar during the las t 
five years;  
 
(c) whether the Government proposes to establish new high -capacity grid 
substations and transmission lines in the Kosi-Seemanchal region of Bihar, if so, 
the details thereof; and  
 
(d) the time-frame fixed for implementation of such projects? 
 
A N S W E R 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF POWER  
 
(SHRI SHRIPAD NAIK)  
 
(a): Government of India has taken the following actions to increase power 
generation, transmission and distribution capacity in the country: 
 
 1. Generation and Storage Planning: 
 
(i) As per National Electricity Plan (Generation), installed generation 
capacity in 2031 -32 is likely to be 874 GW. With a view to ensure 
generation capacity remains ahead of projected demand, all the States, 
in consultation with CEA, have prepared their “Resource Adequacy Plans 
(RAPs)”, which are dynamic 10 -year rolling plans and includes power 
generation as well as power procurement planning. 
 

(ii) All the States were advised to initiate process for creating/ contracting 
generation capacities; from al l generation sources, as per their 
Resource Adequacy Plans. 
 
(iii)   In order to augment the power generation capacity, the Government of 
India has initiated following capacity addition programme:  
 
a.  Thermal Capacity Addition: The projected thermal (coal and lignite) 
capacity requirement by the year 2035 –36 is estimated at approximately 
3,15,000 MW as against the 2,11,855 MW installed capacity as on 
31.03.2023. To meet this requirement, Ministry of Power has envisaged to 
set up an additional minimum 1,05,000 M W coal and lignite based thermal 
capacity. 
 
  Accordingly, Thermal capacities of around 21,080 MW have been 
commissioned since April 2023 till 30.06.2026. In addition, 47,545 MW of 
thermal capacity (including 4,845 MW of stressed thermal power projects) 
is currently under construction. The contracts of 16,000 MW have been 
awarded and are due for construction.  
 
 b.  Central Electricity Authority (CEA) has projected hydro power 
capacity addition of about 16,448 MW during the period 2026 –27 to 2031–
32. Of this, 400 MW has been commissioned as on 30.06.2026 and 12,973 
MW are presently under construction. 
  
 c.  Nuclear Capacity Addition: 8,000 MW of Nuclear Capacity is under 
construction and targeted to be completed by 2031-32. 5,600 MW of Nuclear 
Capacity is under various stages of planning and approval. 
 
 d.  Renewables Capacity Addition: 1,47,720 MW Renewable Capacity 
including 119,580 MW of Solar (including Hybrid -Solar) and 27,720 MW of 
Wind (including Hybrid -wind) is under construction while 47,830 MW of 
Renewable Capacity including 44,440 MW of Solar is at various stages of 
planning and targeted to be completed by 2029-30.   
 
    e.  Addition of Energy Storage Systems:  As on 30.06.2026, 15,870 
MW/95,220 MWh Pumped Storage Projects (PSPs) are under constru ction. 
Further, a total of 6,580 MW/39,480 MWh capacity of Pumped Storage 
Projects (PSPs) are concurred and yet to be taken up for construction. As 
on 30.06.2026, 15,754 MW / 42,530 MWh Battery Energy Storage System 
(BESS) capacity are under construction, 11,747 MW / 38,425 MWh has been 
awarded and 19,192 MW / 67,574 MWh BESS capacity are under tendering 
stage. 
 
2. Promotion of Renewable Energy (RE) Generation:  
 
(i) 100% Inter State Transmission System (ISTS) charges have been waived 
for inter -state sale of so lar and wind power for projects to be 
commissioned by 30th June 2025 (with waiver tapering off 25% annually 
till June 2028), for co -located BESS projects commissioned by June 

2028, for Hydro PSP projects where construction work awarded by June 
2028, for Gr een Hydrogen Projects commissioned till December 2030 
and for offshore wind projects commissioned till December 2032. 
 
 
(ii) Standard Bidding Guidelines for tariff based competitive bidding process 
for procurement of Power from Grid Connected Solar, Wind, Wind -Solar 
Hybrid and Firm & Dispatchable RE (FDRE) projects have been issued. 
 
(iii) Renewable Energy Implementing Agencies (REIAs) are regularly inviting 
bids for procurement of RE power.  
 
(iv) Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) has been permitted up to 100 percent 
under the automatic route.  
 
(v) To augment transmission infrastructure needed for steep RE trajectory, 
transmission plan has been prepared till 2032. 
 
(vi) Laying of new intrastate transmission lines and creating new sub-station 
capacity has been supported under the Gre en Energy Corridor Scheme 
for evacuation of renewable power. 
 
(vii) Scheme for setting up of Solar Parks and Ultra Mega Solar Power projects 
is being implemented to provide land and transmission to RE developers 
for installation of RE projects at large scale. 
 
(viii) Schemes such as Pradhan Mantri Kisan Urja Suraksha evam Utthaan 
Mahabhiyan (PM -KUSUM), PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana, National 
Programme on High Efficiency Solar PV Modules, New Solar Power 
Scheme (for Tribal and PVTG Habitations/Villages) under Pradhan Mantri 
Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan (PM JANMAN) and Dharti Aabha 
Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan (DA JGUA), National Green Hydrogen 
Mission, Viability Gap Funding (VGF) Scheme for Offshore Wind Energy 
Projects have been launched. 
 
(ix) To encourage RE consu mption, Renewable Purchase Obligation (RPO) 
followed by Renewable Consumption Obligation (RCO) trajectory has 
been notified till 2029-30. The RCO which is applicable to all designated 
consumers under the Energy Conservation Act, 2001 will attract 
penalties on non-compliance.  
 
(x)  “Strategy for Establishment of Offshore Wind Energy Projects” has been 
issued. 
 
(xi) Green Term Ahead Market (GTAM) has been launched to facilitate sale of 
Renewable Energy Power through exchanges. 
 
(xii) Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme has been launched to achieve 
the objective of localization of supply chain for solar PV Modules. 

 
 
 
3. Transmission: 
 
  Inter and Intra -State Transmission System has been planned and 
implementation of the same is taken up in matching time frame of genera tion 
capacity addition. As per the National Electricity Plan (Transmission), about 
1,91,474 ckm of transmission lines and 1,274 GVA of transformation capacity is 
planned to be added (at 220 kV and above voltage level) during the ten-year period 
from 2022-23 to 2031-32. 
 
   In addition to the above, the Ministry of Power has issued guidelines dated 
14.06.2024, 21.03.2025 and 15.12.2025 regarding the payment of compensation 
for Right of Way (RoW) for transmission lines, wherein the land rate has been 
linked to the prevailing market rate. These guidelines address the key challenges 
of RoW arising from landowners demanding higher compensation than the rates 
determined by the State Government 
 
4.  Distribution : 
 
     Government of India has supplemented the effo rts of the States earlier 
through schemes like Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gram Jyoti Yojana (DDUGJY), 
Integrated Power Development Scheme (IPDS), Pradhan Mantri Sahaj Bijli Har 
Ghar Yojana (SAUBHAGYA) and currently under Revamped Distribution Sector 
Scheme (RDSS ), to help them achieve the objective of providing quality and 
reliable supply of power. 
 
  Government of India launched RDSS in July 2021 with the objective of 
improving the quality and reliability of power supply to consumers through a 
financially sustai nable and operationally efficient distribution Sector. The 
scheme has an outlay of Rs. 3,03,758 Cr. and estimated Gross Budgetary Support 
(GBS) from Central Government of Rs. 97,631 Cr. Under the scheme, financial 
assistance is being provided to the Distribution Utilities (excluding Private Sector 
Utilities) for loss reduction infrastructure works and smart metering works. 
Projects worth Rs. 1.53 lakh crore for loss reduction infrastructure and Rs. 1.31 
lakh crore for smart metering works have been sanction ed under the scheme 
which would help improve the reliability and quality of power supply in the 
country. 
 
 In addition to above, to support the power distribution utilities to improve 
their Aggregate Technical and Commercial (AT&C) losses some of the key 
initiatives taken, in addition to RDSS, are as under: 
 
(i) Additional Borrowing consent of 0.5% of Gross Sate Domestic Product 
(GSDP) to State Governments, which is conditional on them undertaking 
specific reforms in the power sector.  
 

(ii)  Additional Prudential N orms for sanctioning of loans to State owned 
power utilities contingent on the performance of power distribution 
utilities against prescribed conditions. 
 
(iii) Rules for implementation of Fuel and Power Purchase Cost Adjustment 
(FPPCA) and cost reflective tarif f so as to ensure that all prudent cost 
for supply of electricity is passed through. 
 
(iv)  Rules and Standard Operating Procedure issued for proper subsidy 
accounting and their timely payment. 
 
(b): The details of the projects sanctioned for the development of  power 
generation, transmission and distribution infrastructure in Bihar during the last 
five years are given below: 
 
I. Generation:  
 
 The detail of thermal power project sanctioned in the state of Bihar in the 
last five years is given at Annexure-I. No Hydroelectric projects / Pumped Storage 
Projects in the state of Bihar were concurred by Central Electricity Authority 
(CEA) during the last 5 years. In addition, no nuclear project has been planned in 
the last five years. 
 
II. Transmission:  
 
 To cater to the future, Inter State Transmission System (ISTS) requirements 
in the State of Bihar, about 1,016 ckm transmission lines along with 
reconductoring of about 468 ckm, about 8,200 MVA transformation capacity 
augmentation, and 500 MW HVDC back -to-back refurbi shment/upgradation at 
Pusauli are under construction / under planning. The details of major schemes 
under ISTS which have been approved in last five years along with its 
implementation status viz. completed, under construction, under bidding & under 
planning are as under: 
 
1. ISTS Substations (S/s) Completed: 
 
i. Creation of 220 kV level at existing 400/132 kV Banka (New) (POWERGRID), 
 
ii. Creation of 220 kV level at existing 400/132 kV Lakhisarai (New) 
(POWERGRID). 
 
2. Under construction: 
 
i. Reconductoring of Kaha lgaon – Farakka 400 kV Double circuit (D/c) line 
with High Tension Low Sag (HTLS) conductor:  
 
ii. Upgradation of Pusauli 1x500 MW HVDC (High Voltage Direct Current) 
Back-to-Back to 2x500 MW with SiC VSC (Silicon Carbide Voltage Source 
Converter) based HVDC Back-to-Back:  
 
iii. Diameter completion at Sasaram (POWERGRID) S/s  

  
 
 
3.  Under bidding: 
 
Establishment of Nawada (ISTS) 765/400/220 kV S/s including associated 
lines viz. LILO of Gaya – Balia 765 kV Single circuit (S/c) line at Nawada 
(ISTS) S/s & Na wada (ISTS) – Durgapur (New) – Jeerat (ISTS) 765 kV D/c 
line. 
 
Further, it is to mention that ISTS augmentation is being carried out on 
continuous basis in Bihar commensurate with generation addition, demand 
growth, and as per drawl requirement of state from ISTS network. 
     
III. Distribution:  
 
Under RDSS Scheme, works of Rs. 10,559 Crores for distribution 
infrastructure works and Rs. 2,021 Crores for smart metering works have been 
sanctioned for the State of Bihar. Sanctioned distribution infrastructure  works 
include upgradation / augmentation of sub-stations and distribution transformers, 
upgrading of conductors, laying of ABC / covered conductors, segregation of 
mixed-load feeders, etc. All the distribution schemes are scheduled to be 
completed within sanctioned period i.e. by 31stMarch, 2028. 
 
(c) & (d) :  As per the Resource Adequacy Plan (Transmission) for Bihar, the 
details of upcoming grid substations and transmission lines in the Kosi -
Seemanchal region of Bihar along with tentative time frame is g iven at     
Annexure-II.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA  
MINISTRY OF JAL SHAKTI 
DEPARTMENT OF DRINKING WATER & SANITATION 
  
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3210 
 ANSWERED ON 06/08/2026 
PROGRESS OF JJM IN BARAMULLA 
 
3210. SHRI ABDUL RASHID SHEIKH: 
Will the Minister of JAL SHAKTI be pleased to state: 
(a) the details of the physical and financial progress of Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) and JJM 2.0 in 
Baramulla Lok Sabha Constituency; 
(b) the percentage and the number of Functional Household Tap Connections (FHTCs)  
provided thereunder; and 
(c) the timeline fixed for completion of remaining schemes? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR JAL SHAKTI 
(SHRI V. SOMANNA)  
(a) to (c) Drinking Water is a ‘State’ subject, and therefore,  the responsibility of planning, approval, 
implementation, operation & maintenance of drinking water supply schemes including those under Jal 
Jeevan Mission (JJM) lies with State/UT Governments. The Government of India supports the States 
by providing technical and financial assistance for the implementation of the mission.  
Since August 2019, Government of India, in partnership with States/UTs including Jammu & 
Kashmir, has been implementing JJM – Har Ghar Jal to make provision of tap water supply to every  
rural household of the country. In March 2026, the Union Cabinet has approved extension of the JJM 
up to December 2028, with an enhanced outlay and a restructured implementation framework focusing 
on structural reforms in the rural drinking water supply sector under JJM 2.0.  
As informed by UT of Jammu & Kashmir, approximately 77% (2,44,337) of the total 3,18,600 
households have been provided with tap water connection as on date in Baramulla Lok Sabha 
constituency. Further, there are 525 water supply schem es in Baramulla constituency with an 
estimated cost of Rs. 2,073.50 crore and an expenditure of amount Rs.1,233.28 crore have been made. 
Of these 525 schemes, 250 schemes have been physically completed, while the remaining 275 
schemes are at various stages of execution. These schemes are expected to be completed by December 
2028, in accordance with the timeline of extension of JJM 2.0. 
Under JJM, this Department releases funds to States/UTs only. Further, district -wise fund allocations 
are made and maintain ed by State/UTs Governments. Under first phase of JJM, the UT of Jammu & 
Kashmir was allocated Rs. 18,514.25 crore, of which only Rs.6,496.48 crore was drawn. Under JJM 
2.0, for the FY 2026 -27, the UT has been allocated Rs.905.74 crore, of which mother san ction of 
amount Rs.116.06 crore has been issued to the UT.

  GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3212 
ANSWERED ON 06th AUGUST, 2026 
ILLEGAL COLLECTION FROM VEHICLES ON NHs 
3212. DR. PRASHANT YADAORAO PADOLE: 
Will the Minister of ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
सड़क परिवहन औि िाजमार्ग मंत्री 
be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has received complaints regarding illegal 
collection of money  from commercial vehicles on National Highways, 
particularly in the name of "Mechanical Pass" or  other unauthorized 
charges, if so, the details thereof; 
(b) whether the Government has identified National Highway stretches 
where such illegal  collections and harassment of transporters are 
frequently reported and if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether the Government has issued any guidelines or directions to 
NHAI, concessionaires  and enforcement agencies to prevent 
unauthorized collections and ensure smooth movement of  commercial 
vehicles; and 
(d) the details of the action taken or proposed to be taken by the 
Government t o eliminate  such illegal practices and safeguard the 
interests of transporters?  

2 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
(SHRI NITIN JAIRAM GADKARI) 
(a) User fee at fee plazas on National Highways is collected only in 
accordance with the provisions of the National Highways Fee 
(Determination of Rates and Collection) Rules, 2008 and the respective 
Concession Agreements. 
No such pass, namely "Mechanical Pass", is issued to commercial 
vehicles at National Highway fee plazas. 
(b)  No such Nati onal Highway stretch has been identified for illegal 
collection. 
(c) The Government has issued various instructions and Standard 
Operating Procedures (SOPs) to ensure transparency and operational 
integrity in user fee collection at National Highway fee pla zas. In this 
regard, the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) has issued a 
Standard Operating Procedure dated 25.01.2024 for Operational 
Transparency in Tolling Operations, which provides for surprise 
inspections and regular monitoring to ensure tha t all cash and FASTag 
transactions are processed only through the Toll Management System 
Software. 
(d) To ensure operational integrity, transparency and safeguard the 
interest of road users in user fee collection on National Highways, the 
Government has implemented FASTag -based Electronic Toll Collection 
system. Presently, approximately more than 98% of  user fee collection 
takes place through FASTag under National Electronic Toll Collection 
(NETC) program. All the FASTag transactions are processed in a secured 
ecosystem involving Toll Management System Software, Acquirer Bank 
at fee plaza, National Payme nt Corporation of India (NPCI) as Central 
Clearing House (CCH) and FASTag Issuer Bank. The transaction involves 
a transparent process wherein the deducted user fee (Toll) is informed to 
the highway users and recorded in a central repository. The Electronic  
Toll Collection (ETC) system is designed in such a way that no FASTag 

3 
 
transaction can take place without the participation of all three 
stakeholders i.e., Acquirer Bank at user fee plaza, NPCI and Issuer Bank. 
In order to ensure the smooth functioning of fee plazas and enhance 
transparency, the Government has discontinued cash collection at all NH 
fee plazas with effect from April 2026. Accordingly, User Fee is being 
collected through FASTag/UPI only. 
Further, In order to enhance toll operations and enable  seamless 
movement of vehicles, the Government has adopted a phased rollout of 
Multi-Lane Free Flow (MLFF) user fee collection on 4 -lane and above 
National Highways, based on the outcomes and efficacy of the awarded 
projects. Under the MLFF tolling system,  gantry-mounted high -
performance Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) readers and 
Automatic Number Plate Recognition (ANPR) cameras are used for the 
deduction of user fees through the existing FASTag system,  thereby 
eliminating manual intervention or cash  handling at fee collection 
points. This facilitates barrier -less tolling, wherein user fees are 
collected from vehicle users without requiring them to stop, slow down, 
or remain in a designated lane.  
The Government, through NHAI Rajmarg Yatra App, takes prompt 
corrective action in cases of any complaints, violations, including 
issuance of show -cause notices and penalties as per the applicable 
contractual provisions.

MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS 
 (SHRI SURESH GOPI) 
(a) to (c): Distribution of LPG in Lakshadweep islands is currently done by Indian Oil 
Corporation Limited (IOCL) through Lakshadweep Co-operative Marketing Federation 
(LCMF), designated as the wholesale agent of Lakshadweep Administration under Public 
Distribution System. 
The Retail Selling Price of domestic LPG at Kochi as on 31.07.2026 is Rs. 949 per 14.2 Kg 
cylinder. While the pricing of Lakshadweep is based on Kochi market in Kerala, additional 
transportation and handling charges for bringing the cylinder to various islands of the UT are 
charged from consumers by LCMF. As a result, the Retail Selling Price of domestic LPG in 
Lakshadweep islands is higher than that of Kochi. 
The Retail Selling Prices in various islands of Lakshadweep vary from island to island based 
on the expenditure incurred on placement of cylinders by Lakshadweep Co-operative 
Marketing Federation (LCMF). The amount of expenditure incurred on transportation 
charges, handling and port charges, etc. is worked out by LCMF and is charged from LPG 
consumers. 
To ensure seamless LPG supplies in Lakshadweep islands, IOCL has hired two marine 
vessels MV Elikalpeni and MV Ganga for placement of LPG cylinders at various islands of 
Lakshadweep, incurring additional costs which are currently being borne by IOCL.

3217.   SHRI AJAY BHATT: 
 
Will the Minister of MICRO, SMALL AND MEDIUM ENTERPRISES be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether the Government has launched the Udyam Sakhi Portal to promote self -reliance 
among women in the country and if so, the details thereof; 
(b)  whether any budgetary allocation has been made for the said Portal and if so, the details 
thereof; 
(c)  the total number of beneficiaries who have availed benefits through the said Portal, year -
wise and State-wise; 
(d) whether the Government has launched any scheme for the economic  
empowerment of women entrepreneurs and women -led startups and if so,   
the details thereof along with the number of women beneficiaries under the  
said scheme, State-wise; and 
(e) the details of the funds allocated and utilised under the said project till date across the country 
including in Uttarakhand? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR MICRO, SMALL AND MEDIUM ENTERPRISES 
 (SUSHRI SHOBHA KARANDLAJE) 
 
(a), (b), (c) & (e):  The Udyam Sakhi Portal was conceptualized and launched in 2018 to promote 
women entrepreneurship by providing a digital platform offering information on Government 
schemes, policies, programmes, business planning, financial assistance, mentoring, training, 
exhibitions and other support services to enable women to establish and expand their enterprises. An 
expenditure of ₹43.52 lakh was incurred towards the development of the Portal in 2018. Thereafter, 
no separate budgetary allocation or project -wise fund allocation/utili sation has been made for the 
Udyam Sakhi Portal. A total of 4580 women entrepreneurs had registered on the Portal, and the 
State-wise details of beneficiaries, including Uttarakhand are placed at Annexure-I. 
 
Subsequently, in view of the Government's effor ts to mainstream support for women 
entrepreneurs through a unified digital ecosystem comprising the Udyam Registration Portal (URP), 
Udyam Assist Platform (UAP) and the Ministry's Yashasvini Initiative, the objectives of the Udyam 
Sakhi Portal have been subsumed under these platforms. Accordingly, the Udyam Sakhi Portal has 
been discontinued and a communication in this regard has been issued vide OM dated 01.01.2026. 
Women entrepreneurs registered on the Udyam Sakhi Portal have been onboarded to the Udyam 
Registration Portal/Udyam Assist Platform. 
  
(d):  Ministry of MSME has launched several schemes for the economic empowerment of 
MSMEs (including women owned MSMEs) such as Prime Minister's Employment Generation 
Programme (PMEGP), Credit Guarantee Fund Trus t for Micro and Small Enterprises (CGTMSE), 
IC Scheme, Coir Vikas Yojana, SFURTI, ESDP and other interventions. The State -wise details of 
registered beneficiaries under the said scheme are placed as Annexure-II.

UNSTARRED QUESTION No. 3219 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 6th August, 2026 
 
DIESEL PURCHASE LIMIT FOR FARMERS 
 
 
† 3219. SHRI KULDEEP INDORA: 
 
पेᮝोिलयम और ᮧाक ृ ितक गैस मंᮢी 
 
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has taken cognizance of the hardship faced by farmers in major 
agricultural belts, including Sri Ganganagar and Hanumangarh, due to the 200-litre purchase 
limit on diesel for agricultural activities, affecting Kharif season cultivation and irrigation, if so, 
the details thereof; 
(b) whether the Government has conducted an assessment of the actual diesel requirements of 
farmers for operating tractors, harvesters, irrigation pumps and other agricultural machinery, if 
so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether the Government proposes to review the agricultural diesel purchase ceiling to  
restore adequate supplies as before; and 
(d) if so, the details thereof along with the proposed timeline for its implementation? 
 
ANSWER 
 
पेᮝोिलयम और ᮧाक ृ ितक गैस मंᮢालय मᱶ रा᭔यमंᮢी 
(᮰ी सुरेश गोपी) 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS 
(SHRI SURESH GOPI) 
 
(a) to (d) : Owing to the West Asia Crisis, International Crude Oil prices increased sharply. To 
protect retail consumers, though the full increase in the price of High-Speed Diesel (HSD) was 
passed on to bulk consumers, only a partial increase was passed on to retail consumers resulting 
in a significant price differential between bulk price and retail price of HSD. This resulted into 
uneven extraordinary demand growth in some retail outlets due to shifting of bulk diesel volume 
to PSU Oil Marketing Retail Outlets (ROs). This was driven by industrial, commercial and 
institutional consumers shifting their procurement from their dedicated consumer pumps to  ROs 
due to the said price difference between bulk and retail diesel prices.  The diversion of HSD by 
bulk consumers led to localized supply issues and potential disruptions for bona fide retail 
consumers and essential services.  
 
To address this situation and to ensure the availability and equitable distribution of HSD, the 
Central Government notified the Motor Spirit and High-Speed Diesel (Temporary Regulation of 
Supply through Retail Outlets) Order, 2026 on 11.06.2026 and on 12.06.2026, it issued 
directions to PSU OMCs introducing temporary restrictions on Sale of HSD from their 
RetailOutlets.  These measures were aimed at preventing black marketing, hoarding and 
diversion of HSD while ensuring uninterrupted availability of MS and HSD to retail consumers.  
 
Following a review of the supply situation of petroleum products in the country, the 
Government decided to withdraw the temporary restrictions in public interest   w.e.f. 1st July 
2026 thereby restoring the normal supply arrangements of MS and HSD across the country 
including Ganganagar and Hanumangarh.

(a) whether the discovery of new oil and natural gas reserves or the presence of hydrocarbons in 
Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, Bihar, Andaman and other areas has been confirmed in recent years, if 
so, the details thereof; 
(b) the areas where commercial production is likely to commence on the basis of such discoveries 
and the time by which the same is likely to commence; 
(c) the extent to which the country's domestic production of oil and natural gas and its import 
dependence are likely to be reduced through such discoveries; and 
(d) whether the Government is taking any special initiatives to expedite the exploration of new oil 
and natural gas fields in the country, if so, the details thereof?

MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS 
(SHRI SURESH GOPI) 
 
 
(a)      28 hydrocarbon discoveries have been notified during the last 3 years. 
(b)    Hydrocarbon discoveries undergo a series of technical and commercial evaluations before 
commencement of commercial production. These include appraisal drilling,reservoir studies, 
extended well testing, preparation of Field Development Plan (FDP), obtaining statutory and 
environmental clearances and development drilling along with installation of production 
facilities. The commencement of commercial production depends upon the successful completion 
of all these activities and the commercial viability of the discoveries. 
(c)     The contribution of newly discovered hydrocarbon fields to domestic oil and natural gas 
production can be assessed only after completion of appraisal activities, estimation of 
recoverable reserves, approval of Field Development Plans (FDPs) and commencement of 
commercial production.

natural gas fields in the country the details are placed at Annexure-I.

FOREIGN MEDICAL GRADUATE EXAMINATION (FMGE)
3222. DR. T SUMATHY ALIAS THAMIZHACHI THANGAPANDIAN:
Will the Minister of HEALTHAND FAMILYWELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Government has taken cognizance of complaints about the rising difficulty
level and low pass rates in the recently conducted Foreign Medical Graduate Examination
(FMGE), if so, the details thereof;
(b) whether the Government has assessed whether the current examination pattern, syllabus
alignment and question design are disproportionately affecting genuine foreign medical
graduates, if so, the details thereof;
(c) the details of the steps the Government has taken or planning to take to improve
transparency, predictability and fairness in the FMGE while maintaining standards;
(d) whether the Government proposes to undertake any review of the FMGE framework in
consultation with the National Medical Commission and other stakeholders; and
(e) if so, the details thereof?
ANSWER
THE MINISTER OF STATEIN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILY
WELFARE
(SMT. ANUPRIYAPATEL)
(a) to (e): The Foreign Medical Graduate Examination (FMGE) is conducted by the National
Board of Examinations in Medical Sciences (NBEMS) in accordance with the provisions of
the Screening Test Regulations for Foreign Medical Graduates (FMGs) seeking provisional or
permanent registration with the National Medical Commission (NMC) or the respective State
Medical Councils (SMCs). The pass rate in FMGE depends on multiple factors including the
quality of medical education imparted, individual candidate's level of knowledge and
performance in the examination.
The Syllabus for the FMGE comprises Subjects/Knowledge Areas as per the Competency
based Undergraduate Curriculum published by NMC for the MBBS Course. Further, the
questions for FMGE are developed through structured Question Banking and Item Writing
workshops followed by Validation Workshops by a different group of subject experts. Each
question is reviewed for content accuracy, relevance to the approved syllabus, reliability and
validity. The overall process ensures that the examination maintains the expected standards of

MBBS graduate and assesses the knowledge and competence required for safe medical
practice in the Indian healthcare system.
The FMGE is conducted strictly in accordance with the notified regulations and prescribed
qualifying criteria. Any changes relating to the eligibility criteria, syllabus or regulatory
framework governing FMGs are considered by the NMC from time to time in accordance
with the statutory provisions and stakeholder requirements.

CAPITAL DREDGING PROJECTS FOR DIU PORT 
  
3224.      SHRI PATEL UMESHBHAI BABUBHAI: 
  
    Will the Minister of PORTS, SHIPPING AND WATERWAYS be pleased to state: 
पȅन, पोत पįरवहन और जलमागŊ मंũी 
 
  
(a)       whether the Government is aware that the Capital Dredging Projects for Diu 
Port and Vanakbara Creek in the Union Territory of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and 
Daman and Diu under the Sagarmala Programme have not commenced due to non-
granting of financial approval/ release of funds despite getting the technical approval 
and completion of the necessary administrative and tender processes; 
(b)       if so, the reasons therefor; 
(c)        whether administrative and financial responsibility will be fixed for delay in 
according financial approval which leads to increase in project cost or have to adopt 
re-tendering, re-evaluation or other administrative procedure resulting in additional 
loss of time and public funds as well as inconvenience to the local people, if so, the 
details thereof including the officers/department against whom the responsibility will 
be fixed; 
(d)       whether the Government proposes to formulate any time-bound action plan for 
granting early financial approval and releasing funds for the said two projects; and 
(e)       if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor? 
  
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF PORTS, SHIPPING AND WATERWAYS 
(SHRI SARBANANDA SONOWAL) 
  
(a) to (e):        Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways (MoPSW) conveyed in-
principle approval in October, 2018 for the projects ‘Dredging at Vanakbara Port of UT 
of Daman and Diu’ and ‘Dredging at Diu Port of UT of Daman and Diu’ at estimated 
cost of ₹ 46.44 crore and ₹ 45.90 crore with financial assistance of ₹ 23.22 crore and 

₹ 22.95 crore under Sagarmala scheme respectively. However, the projects could not 
be executed by the Union Territory (UT) Administration of Dadra and Nagar Haveli 
and Daman and Diu (DNH&DD), the executing agency, for more than five years. 
Therefore, in order to maintain fiscal discipline under Sagarmala scheme, the projects 
were de-sanctioned by the MoPSW on 04.06.2024.  
Subsequently, UT Administration of DNH&DD approached MoPSW in 
November, 2024 for administrative approval and expenditure sanction of the projects 
at revised estimated cost of ₹ 80.29 crore and ₹ 81.34 crore respectively. However, 
on account of fiscal constraint in the current Sagarmala scheme during the 15th 
Finance Commission cycle, the projects could not be accommodated. 
  
The sanction of financial assistance by MoPSW for these two projects is 
contingent upon the approval of Sagarmala 2.0 scheme. Separately, the UT 
Administration can always execute these projects out of its own budget to avoid any 
delay.

TO BE ANSWERED ON 07TH AUGUST, 2026
REVIEW OF FOOD SAFETY AND STANDARDS ACT
3225. SHRI AMRINDER SINGH RAJA WARRING:
Will the Minister of HEALTHAND FAMILYWELFAREbe pleased to state:
(a) whether any review of the existing framework of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006,
has been carried out by the Government recently given the inadequacy of the existing penal
framework, the shortage of Food Safety Officers, ineffective laboratory infrastructure, delays
in adjudication, non-recovery of penalties and widespread licensing irregularities, if so, the
details thereof;
(b) whether the Government is aware that the Supreme Court has recently taken notice of the
said issue, if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the steps taken by the Government to address the growing national concerns regarding
food adulteration, contamination, misleading labelling, unsafe packaged food products and
inadequate enforcement of food safety standards across the country?
ANSWER
THE MINISTER OF STATEIN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILY
WELFARE
(SHRI PRATAPRAOJADHA V)
(a) to (c): Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) is mandated to lay down
science-based standards for articles of food and to regulate their manufacture, storage,
distribution, sale and import to ensure availability of safe and wholesome food for human
consumption. The implementation and enforcement of the Food Safety and Standards (FSS)
Act, 2006 is a shared responsibility between the Central and State Governments.
To strengthen food safety enforcement, FSSAI regularly reviews the performance and
vacancies of Food Safety Officers of all States/UTs through various forums like Central
Advisory Committee (CAC) meetings, Inter-State Zonal Council Meetings.
For the safety of the food and food products through testing, FSSAI has notified a
network of 259 NABL accredited food testing laboratories comprising laboratories of
State/UT Governments, Government institutions, and NABL-accredited private laboratories
for the analysis of food samples. FSSAI has also notified 24 Referral Food Laboratories for
the analysis of appeal samples. There are also 305 Mobile Food Testing Laboratories (Food

Safety on Wheels) deployed across the country to conduct on-the-spot testing, distribute rapid
kits, and drive public awareness in remote areas.
SoFTeL scheme (Strengthening of Food Testing System in the Country including
provision of Mobile Food Testing Labs) is an initiative implemented by the FSSAI to upgrade
state food labs, set up microbiology facilities, and deploys mobile food testing vans. Under
this scheme, 47 State Food Testing Laboratories have been structurally upgraded with
advanced analytical equipment.
Around 98% of the Food Business Operators (FBOs) fall within the jurisdiction of the
State/UT Food Safety Authorities. Accordingly, the enforcement and implementation of the
provisions of the FSS Act, 2006 primarily rests with the State/UT Food Safety Authorities
within their respective jurisdictions. To ensure compliance with the standards, limits, and
other statutory requirements prescribed under the FSS Act, 2006, and the regulations made
thereunder, the State Food Safety Authorities undertake regular surveillance, monitoring,
targeted enforcement drives, inspections, and sampling activities across the food sector.
Court cases whenever filed are responded mentioning the provisions of FSS Act, 2006
and regulations made thereunder from time to time.
FSSAI has launched various campaigns such as “#No To Adulteration” & “How to
Check for Adulteration” video on its official YouTube channel campaign to raise consumer
awareness about food adulteration and how to identify adulterated products;
"#HarLabelKuchKahtaHai" (Every Label Speaks) campaign to empower citizens with label
literacy for healthier eating and informed choices. This initiative educates consumers on key
elements like nutritional information (calories, fats, sugars, protein), ingredient lists, allergen
warnings, and date markings. These initiatives include advertisements, educational materials,
and online platforms to spread awareness.
FSSAI has introduced DART (Detect Adulteration with Rapid Test) book which
covers 44 tests that can be performed easily at households with the help of water and simple
solutions like tincture of iodine for food products such as Milk & Milk Products, Oils, Sugar
& Confectionary, Food Grains & its products, Spices & Condiments. These tests also include
sensory evaluation tests for establishing authentication of food products. DART book depicts
differences between pure and adulterated food product through pictorial representation. The
same is available on FSSAI Website.
Also, Food Safety Magic Box is a compact and user-friendly kit containing simple,
rapid test methods to detect common food adulterants in seven types of food commodities.
This kit is used and distributed in schools as part of food safety awareness initiative. It aims
to engage students through hands-on learning, enabling them to identify adulteration in
everyday food items such as milk, spices, oils, and grains.

Act, 2006 is a shared responsibility between the Central and State Governments.
FSSAI has funded the project by CSIR-Indian Institute of Toxicology Research,
Lucknow, ICAR-Central institute of Fisheries Technology (ICAR-CIFT), Kochi and Birla
Institute of Technology and Science (BITS), Pilani titled "Micro-and nano-plastics as
emerging food contaminants: Establishing validated Methodologies and understanding the
prevalence in different food matrices". The objectives of the project are:-
i. Development and validation of analytical methods for identification and
quantification of micro/nano-plastics in foods matrices.

ii. Inter- and intra-laboratory comparison of developed methods in identified food
matrices.
iii. Surveillance and determination of exposure levels of micro-/nano-plastics in
identified foods matrices.
FSSAI has also notified the Food Safety and Standards (Packaging) Regulations, 2018,
wherein, requirements for food-grade packaging are specified. It mandates that any material
which comes in direct contact with food or likely to come in contact with food used for
packaging, preparation, storing, wrapping, transportation and sale or service of food shall be
of food grade quality. It also prescribes standards for plastic materials intended to come into
contact with food products, which makes reference to the corresponding Bureau of Indian
Standards (BIS) specifications. These standards are on par with international standards,
thereby ensuring consistency with global food safety practices. Further, it specifies that all
packaging materials of plastic origin shall pass the prescribed overall migration limit of
60mg/kg or 10mg/dm2 when tested as per IS 9845 with no visible colour migration.
The Food Safety and Standards (Packaging) Regulations, 2018 also specifies that every
food business operator shall obtain the certificate of conformity issued by National
Accreditation Board for Testing and Calibration Laboratories (NABL) against these
regulations for the packaging material which comes in direct contact with food or layers
likely to come in contact with food to be used.

science-based standards for articles of food and to regulate their manufacture, storage,
distribution, sale and import to ensure availability of safe and wholesome food for human
consumption. The implementation and enforcement of the Food Safety and Standards (FSS)
Act, 2006 is a shared responsibility between the Central and State Governments.

FSSAI has established a robust consumer grievance redressal mechanism for
addressing food safety related complaints. Complaints/concerns of consumers and Food
Business Operators (FBO) are received through various channels such as Web portal, Mobile

enforcement drives, inspections, and sampling activities across the food sector.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF AYUSH 
  
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3229 
ANSWERED ON- 07/08/2026 
 
STRENGTHENING OF QUALITY AND TESTING OF AYUSH MEDICINES 
 
3229. SHRI K E PRAKASH 
Will the Minister of AYUSH be pleased to state:- 
 
(a) whether , in the context of the BRICS Traditional, Complementary and Integrative 
Medicine 
(TCIM) initiative, the Union Government has proposed any measures to strengthen quality  
assurance, toxicity testing and the international standardisation of AYUSH medicines, if so, 
the details thereof; 
 
(b) the details of the Central Drug Testing Laboratories, quality-testing facilities or laboratory 
upgradation projects supported in Tamil Nadu during the current year; 
 
(c) whether the Government proposes to strengthen testing infrastructure for AYUSH 
products to facilitate compliance with international quality standards and support exports 
from herbal- 
producing regions, including Tamil Nadu, if so, the details thereof; and 
  
(d) the  measures taken by the Government to promote internationally accepted quality  
certification and scientific validation of AYUSH medicines? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE (IC) OF THE MINISTRY OF AYUSH 
 
 
(SHRI PRATAPRAO JADHAV) 
 
 
(a) During the 16 th BRICS Health Ministers' Meeting held in Chandigarh from 21 st to 24 th 
July, 2026, the BRICS Member States finalized the Terms of Reference (ToR) for the 
establishment of the BRICS Expert Working Group on Traditional, Complementary and 
Integrative Medicine (TCIM) under the BRICS Health Track. The Working Group has been 
established with the following objectives: 
(i) To promote policy dialogue and exchange of experiences; 
(ii) To strengthen collaboration in research and evidence-generation; 
(iii) To enhancing capacity-building, academic exchanges and institutional partnerships; 

(iv) To advance digital co-operation and knowledge-sharing; 
(v) To encourage innovation and exchange of best practices in TCIM; 
(vi)To strengthen cooperation for the  development of policies and mechanisms for  the 
recognition and protection of intellectual property and use rights over the knowledge and care 
technologies of traditional and indigenous peoples; 
(vii) To promote healthy lifestyles and holistic well-being through TCIM approaches. 
(b) Ministry of Ayush , Government of India  is implementing a Central Sector Scheme, 
namely Ayush Oushadhi Gunvatta Evam Uttpadan Samvardhan Yojana (AOGUSY) to 
support Ayush Pharmacies and Drug Testing Laboratories to achieve higher standards like 
World Health Organization Good Manufacturing Practices (WHO -GMP) and National 
Accreditation Board for Testing and Calibration Laboratories (NABL) respectively.  The 
Scheme was approved by Standing Finance Committee (SFC) on 16.03.2021  with total 
budget outlay of Rs. 122.00 crores for five years. 
During the current year i.e. 2026 -27, State Govt. Drug Testing Laboratory, Tamil 
Nadu has been supported under AOGUSY scheme with a G rant-in-Aid of Rs. 68,00,000/- in 
the component namely Strengthening and up -gradation of Ayush Pharmacies and Drug 
Testing Laboratories. 
(c) & (d) The Ministry of Ayush has undertaken following initiatives to strengthen the quality 
ecosystem for Ayush medicines, including support  for quality certification and scientific 
validation to enhance global acceptance and exports of Ayush medicines  across the country  
including Tamil Nadu - 
i. Ministry of Ayush is implementing a Central Sector Scheme, namely, Ayush 
Oushadhi Gunvatta Evam Uttpadan Samvardhan Yojana (AOGUSY) to support 
Ayush Pharmacies and Drug Testing Laboratories to achieve higher standards like 
WHO-GMP and National Accreditation Board for Testing and Calibration 
Laboratories (NABL) respectively. Further, the scheme also supports for development 
of standards and accreditation/certification of Ayush products & materials in 
collaboration with Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS), Quality Council of India (QCI) 
and other relevant scientific institutions and industrial Research & Development 
centres. 
ii. Drug Testing L aboratories are approved by Ministry of Ayush under Rules 160A to 
160J of the Drugs Rules, 1945, for carrying out tests relating to the identity, purity, 
quality and strength of Ayush drugs. As on date, 118 private Drug Testing 
Laboratories have been approved by the Ministry across States and Union Territories 

for conducting such tests in accordance with the provisions of the Drugs Rules, 1945.  
In addition, there are 34 Drug Testing Laboratories available in State/UTs for testing 
of the Legal Samples drawn by the Drug Inspectors of concerned State/UTs. 
iii. The Pharmacopoeia Commission for Indian Medicine & Homoeopathy (PCIM&H), a 
subordinate organization under Ministry of Ayush, develops pharmacopoeial 
standards and formulary specifications for Ayush drugs, which serve as the official 
compendia for determining their identity, purity, and strength. Compliance with these 
standards is mandatory under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940 and the Rules made 
thereunder. PCIM&H also functions as the Appellate Drug Testing Laboratory for 
Ayush drugs and conducts regular capacity-building programmes for Drug Regulatory 
Authorities, Drug Analysts, and other stakeholders on standardization, quality control, 
and testing methodologies to strengthen the quality assurance system for Ayush drugs. 
iv. Ministry of Ayush has  also set up Research Councils for undertaking, coordinating, 
formulating, developing, and promoting research on scientific lines in Ayush 
sciences. The research activities of the councils include Clinical Research, Drug 
Standardization, Pharmacological Research, Medicinal Plant Research, Literary 
Research & Documentation programme, Fundamental research, pharmaceutical 
research and Public Health Research. 
v. WHO Certificate of Pharmaceutical Product (WHO -CoPP) to Ayush drugs is issued 
by Central Drugs Standard Control Organization (CDSCO) after joint inspections of 
manufacturing units by Drug Inspectors posted in Ayush vertical along with drug 
inspectors of State/UTs and CDSCO for compliance with WHO Technical Report 
Series (TRS) guidelines for Herbal Medicines. 
vi. Ministry of Ayush has launched Ayush Quality Mark (AQM) initiative through the 
Ayush Export Promotion Council (AYUSHEXCIL). Under this framework, the 
Ayush Quality Mark is being granted after scrutiny and verification of valid quality 
certifications and statutory approvals issued by the competent Government 
authorities, such as WHO -GMP, Ayush Premium Mark and other recognised 
certifications, as applicable. 
vii. Ayush Standard Mark and Ayush Premium Mark are awarded to Ayush Drugs by 
Quality Council of India (QCI) based on third -party assessment of compliance with 
prescribed national and international quality standards.

IMPLEMENTATION OF NIRBHAYA FUND PROJECTS IN KARNATAKA  
  
3230. SHRI TEJASVI SURYA: 
  
 Will the Minister of WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT  be pleased to state: 
  
(a)  the details of initiatives approved under the Nirbhaya Fund, including Safe City 
Projects, One Stop Centres, Women Help Desks and other interventions, project -wise 
in Karnataka, particularly in Bengaluru Urban, Bengaluru Rural and Mysuru, during 
the last t hree years indicating the implementing agency and the current status of each 
project; 
(b)  the details of funds sanctioned, released and utilised under these initiatives, project -
wise during the last three years, along with the reasons for any delay in 
implementation/under-utilisation of funds; 
(c)  the outcomes achieved under these initiatives, including infrastructure created, Safe 
City interventions operationalised, One Stop Centres established/strengthened, Women 
Help Desks supported, beneficiaries covered and the monitoring indicators used by the  
Government to assess their effectiveness; and  
(d)  the details of the measures taken/proposed to be taken by the Government to expedite 
pending projects and strengthen the implementation and monitoring of Nirbhaya Fund 
initiatives in Karnataka? 
  
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT  
(SHRIMATI SAVITRI THAKUR)  
  
(a) & (b):  Aimed at enhancing the safety and security of women and girls in the country, 
Nirbhaya Fund has been set up as a dedicated non -lapsable corpus fund administered by the 
Department of Economic Affairs (DEA), Ministry of Finance in accordance with the 
framework and guidelines issued by the Government from time to time. The Projects/ Schemes 
under Nirbhaya Fund that have been implemented/ being implemented in the State of 
Karnataka are at Annexure I. The details of funds sanctioned, released and utilised under these 
initiatives, project-wise during the last three years, are at Annexure II.  

Under the Nirbhaya Fund, depending on the requirements for the year and taking in to account 
the balance amount already available in the Public Account of Nirbhaya Fund, Government 
allocates funds on a normative basis in the Annual Budget of the relevant n odal Ministries/ 
Departments.  
(c) In Bengaluru Safe City project, in order to ensure safety of places where women work and 
live, all types of CCTV Surveillance Systems (11000+) installed and integrated, GIS Based 
Crime Mapping Services have been completed, 50 Safety Islands installed a nd integrated, 
Integrated Command and Control Center (ICCC) and an Integrated Support Centre for Women 
and Children have been setup and operationalized, Women Help Desk established in 111 
Police Stations and 08 Hospitals, Women Police Outposts established at 60 locations, 
Upgradation of Karnataka State Police App, Complaint Boxes setup in all 111 police stations, 
8 Forensic Vans with SOC Kits are in operation, Gender Sensitization - Awareness Campaign 
have been conducted in Schools, Prison and Public, 250 Dash Cams procured, 10 Toilet 
facilities in stations and bandobast, 4 Cyber Labs established and 4 batches of Rani Chennama 
Team of highly-trained women police personnel set up.  
To ensure that the Police Stations are more women friendly and approachable, 15,049 Women 
Help Desks (WHDs) have been set up in Police Stations across the country, of which 14,363 
are headed by women police officers. Out of these, 1050 WHDs have been estab lished in 
Karnataka. The officials posted at these Women Help Desks are trained to be sensitive towards 
women and are assisted by a panel of lawyers, psychologists and NGOs for counselling, 
rehabilitation and support services. Furthermore, Karnataka operat es 30 functional FTSCs 
including 16 ePOCSO Courts that have disposed of 17,147 cases. T he number of personnel 
trained in Cybercrime under CCPWC Scheme in Karnataka are 2240 and the State has 
established 35 Anti-Human Trafficking Units. Additionally, 44 OSCs are functioning in 
Karnataka State. Out of which 6 OSCs are located in Bengaluru Urban, 01 in Bengaluru Rural 
and 2 in Mysuru district. The Women Helpline control room is functioning at Bengaluru Urban 
district. OSCs and WHL projects are implemented by the State Government. More than 
1,23,600 women have been assisted via Women Helpline across Karnataka.  
(d) Projects are conceptualized, planned and brought to the Inter Ministerial Empowered 
Committee (EC) for appraisal and recommendation. Upon appraisal and recommendation of 
the proposals by the EC, the sponsoring Ministry’s respective Competent Financial Authority 
(CFA) gives the approval, after which the allocation of funds from the Nirbhaya Fund is made 
in the Budget of the sponsoring Ministry/ Department by the Ministry of Finance. For projects/ 
schemes which require recurring expenditure, funds are released upon receipt of Utilisation 
Certificates (UCs) and Statement of Expenditure (SoE ) from the Implementing 
Ministries/Departments/ State Governments/ UTs, as required, as per provisions of General 
Financial Rules (GFR). The projects/ schemes under Nirbhaya Fund are demand driven and 
generally have staggered implementation schedules and t he responsibility of implementation 
of the project lies with the concerned sponsoring Ministries/Departments/ State Governments.  
The Inter Ministerial Empowered Committee also reviews the status of implementation of 
projects, and expenditure on approved projects from time to time in conjunction with the 

concerned sponsoring Ministries/ Departments/ State Governments/ UTs. The concerned 
Ministries/ Departments/ State Governments/ UTs also monitor the progress of 
implementation at their own levels.

3233. SHRI PRAVEEN PATEL:  
SHRI VISHWESHWAR HEGDE KAGERI:  
SHRI DILIP SAIKIA:  
SHRI RAVINDRA SHUKLA ALIAS RAVI KISHAN: 
  
Will the Minister of PORTS, SHIPPING AND WATERWAYS be pleased to state:  
पƣन, पोत पǐरवहन और जलमाग[ मंğी 
  
(a) the role of lighthouses beyond providing aids to Navigation along with the theme of 
the Lighthouse Tourism Project;  
(b) the manner in which the project aligns with the Government's vision for preserving 
maritime heritage and promoting tourism; and  
(c) the steps being taken by the Directorate General of Lighthouses and Lightships 
(DGLL) to establish lighthouses and promote tourism along inland waterways in the 
North-Eastern region, including site inspections and coordination with IWAI? 
  
ANSWER 
  
MINISTER OF PORTS, SHIPPING AND WATERWAYS 
(SHRI SARBANANDA SONOWAL) 
  
(a) to (c)      Lighthouses primarily serve as Marine Aids to Navigation for ensuring safe 
and efficient maritime navigation. In addition to this core function, the Government is 
actively promoting Lighthouse Tourism which is in line with its vision of preserving India's 
maritime heritage and promoting educational, cultural and tourism purposes under 
Section 23 of the Marine Aids to Navigation Act, 2021. As part of this initiative, Lighthouse 
Museums have been established at Chennai, Mahabalipuram, Alappuzha, Kannur, 
Muttom, Dwarka and Gopnath to showcase the evolution of lighthouse technology and 
India's maritime heritage. Under this initiative, tourism facilities have been developed at 
75 lighthouses across the country as part of the Government's vision to preserve their 
historical and architectural significance. List is attached as Annexure.             

The Directorate General of Lighthouses and Lightships (DGLL) and the Inland 
Waterways Authority of India (IWAI) signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) on

development and establishment of lighthouses on National Waterway-2 (NW-2). Joint 
inspections were carried out by DGLL and IWAI to identify suitable sites for the 
establishment of lighthouses along NW-2. Feasibility studies were conducted based on 
the findings of the site inspections, considering navigational requirements, site 
accessibility, land availability and tourism potential. Based on these feasibility studies, 
four sites, namely Bogibeel, Silghat, Pandu and Biswanath Ghat along NW-2, have been

3234. SHRI PUTTAMAHESH KUMAR:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILYWELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Government has undertaken any study to modernise medical education in the
country;
(b) if so, the details thereof, along with the steps undertaken over the last five years,
especially in this regards to use of emerging and modern technologies in medical colleges and
hospitals across the country;
(c) the details of the total amount of funds allocated, released and utilised to modernise the
curriculum and infrastructure in medical colleges across the country, State-wise particularly in
Andhra Pradesh; and
(d) whether the Government has considered integrating emerging technologies such as artificial
intelligence and blockchain based initiatives into medical education across the country and if so,
the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor?
ANSWER
THE MINISTER OF STATEIN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILY
WELFARE
(SMT. ANUPRIYAPATEL)
(a) to (d): The National Medical Commission (NMC) is an apex statutory body constituted by
an Act of Parliament, entrusted with the responsibility of regulating and overseeing medical
education and practice across the country. The Commission has undertaken comprehensive
measures to modernize the quality of medical education in the country including the
Competency Based Medical Education (CBME) Curriculum, 2024. To fulfill the objective
of CBME, the medical colleges are expected to offer a range of elective options in areas

such as the use of Artificial Intelligence, computers in health and medical education and
ethical use of technology including AI.
Minimum Standard Requirements for Post Graduate Courses (PGMSR-2023) mandates well
equipped departmental and central research laboratories, modern diagnostic and imaging
facilities, digital libraries, access to e-journals and online research databases, high speed
internet and Wi-Fi connectivity in the medical colleges/institutions.
Further, the Postgraduate Medical Education Regulations, 2023 (PGMER 2023) requires
that students maintain digital logbooks for recording clinical work, procedures and academic
activities. Departments are encouraged to promote e-learning and digital documentation as
part of training programme
In addition, the National Board of Examinations in Medical Sciences (NBEMS) has
launched an online training programme on Artificial Intelligence in Medical Education for
healthcare professionals from across the country.
The government has increased number of Medical Colleges, Under Graduate (UG) and Post
Graduate (PG) seats. The number of Medical Colleges have increased from 387 to 846; UG
seats from 51,348 to 1, 39,489 and PG seats from 31,185 to 86,360 from 2014 to as on date.
The Government has implemented following schemes to improve the infrastructure for
Medical education in the country:
 Centrally Sponsored Scheme for establishment of new medical college by
upgrading district/ referral hospital under which 139 new medical colleges are
functional out of 157 approved medical colleges.
 Centrally Sponsored Scheme for strengthening/ upgradation of existing State
Government/Central Government Medical Colleges to increase MBBS and PG
seats.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF LAW AND JUSTICE 
DEPARTMENT OF LEGAL AFFAIRS

TO BE ANSWERED ON FRIDAY, THE 07th AUGUST, 2026 
 
PROGRESS ON LEGISLATIVE REFORMS 
3235. SHRI BALRAM NAIK PORIKA: 
Will the Minister of LAW AND JUSTICE be pleased to state: 
(a) the progress made in legislative reforms, the new laws enacted to promote ease of doing 
business and their implementation status; 
(b) the details of alternate dispute resolution mechanisms (mediation and arbitration) promoted 
and the number of cases resolved; 
(c) the impact on contract enforcement and India’s ranking in World Bank Ease of Doing 
Business parameters; and 
(d) whether any performance audit has been conducted on judicial infrastructure development 
and the timely delivery of justice, if so, the details thereof?” 
  
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE MINISTRY OF 
 LAW AND JUSTICE; AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF 
PARLIAMENTARY AFFAIRS 
 
(SHRI ARJUN RAM MEGHWAL) 
(a): Legislative and policy interventions along with related reforms for promoting ease of doing 
business is a continuous process being undertaken by the Government, keeping in view the 
changing requirements of the stakeholders.  The Government continues to take steps to reduce 
the criminalisation of minor violations and replace them with more proportionate civil penalties 
and administrative mechanisms under various enactments. In this regard, recognising the need 
to make laws more balanced and practical, t he Government began a process of reviewing 
provisions. An important step in this direction was the Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) 
Act, 2023, which removed criminal penalties for a number of minor offences across several 
Central laws. Pursuant theret o, the Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Act, 2026 was 
published in the Official Gazette on 8 April 2026, which rationalizes provisions across 79 

2 
 
Central Acts administered by 23 Ministries and Departments. The reforms are aimed at 
promoting trust -based governance, reducing compliance burden, improving ease of doing 
business, and ensuring proportionate regulatory enforcement. 
(b): The Government continues to promote alternate dispute resolution (ADR) mechanisms 
including arbitration and mediation in the country, as these mechanisms are less adversarial 
and are capable of providing a better substitute to the conventional methods of r esolving 
disputes. The Government is further taking policy and legislative interventions, to strengthen 
these mechanisms and make them more efficacious and expeditious.  
The major initiatives, steps and measures taken by the Central Government over the years in 
this regard include with respect to the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 which has been 
progressively amended in the years 2015, 2019 and 2020 to keep pace wi th current 
developments in the arbitration landscape and to enable arbitration as a viable dispute 
resolution mechanism. The amendments are aimed at ensuring timely conclusion of 
arbitration proceedings, neutrality of arbitrators, minimizing judicial intervention in the arbitral 
process, efficacious enforcement of arbitral awards and promotion of institutional arbitration. 
The Commercial Courts Act, 2015 was also amended in the year 2018 to provide inter-alia for 
Pre-Institution Mediation and Settlement (PIMS) mechanism. Under this mechanism, where a 
commercial dispute of specified value does not contemplate any urgent interim relief, the 
parties have to first exhaust the mandatory remedy of PIMS before approaching the Court. This 
is aimed at providing an opportunity to the parties to resolve the commercial disputes through 
mediation.  
The India International Arbitration Centre Act, 2019, was enacted to provide for the 
establishment of the India International Arbitration Centre for the purpose of creating an 
independent, autonomous and world class body for facilitating institutional arbi tration and to 
declare the Centre to be an institution of national importance. The Centre has since been 
established and aims to inspire confidence amongst parties, both domestic and international, 
by providing a neutral dispute resolution platform for res olution of commercial disputes 
through arbitration.  
The Mediation Act, 2023, lays down the legislative framework for mediation to be adopted by 
disputing parties, especially under the aegis of institutional mediation. The Mediation Act, 2023 
is also expected to be a pivotal legislative intervention towards providing standalone law on 
mediation and enabling the growth of a culture of amicable settlement of disputes out of court. 
Further, the aforesaid interventions from time to time have contributed towards improving and 
strengthening the ADR landscape, supporting the ease of doing business and enabling the 
country being seen as an attractive destination for investments and economic growth. 
The Authorities constituted under the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987 are also promoting 
alternate dispute resolution mechanisms including Mediation.  These Authorities have been 

3 
 
making efforts through legal awareness programmes and to strengthen the court annexed 
mediation as well as Pre Institution Mediation.  
The details of the cases settled by Legal Services Authorities through Mediation in the last two 
years is as under: 
Years Cases settled  
2024-25 98,406 
2025-26 2,25,647 
(c): India has undertaken sustained reforms over the past years to improve its business 
regulatory environment. The government’s focus has gradually shifted from a compliance -
heavy system to a facilitation -driven ecosystem. Reforms have aimed at enhancing speed , 
transparency, and trust-based governance across processes. Consequently, this has resulted in 
growing investor confidence in India’s business environment and improved Ease of Doing 
Business (EoDB).   
In the latest Doing Business Report, 2020 released by the World Bank on 24th October, 2019, 
overall India stands at 63rd position out of 190 countries. Since 2014, India’s rank has gone up 
from 142 to 63 in 2019. However, the EoDB exercise was discontinued by the World Bank in 
the year 2020. 
(d): The Centrally Sponsored Scheme for the Development of Infrastructure Facilities for 
District and Subordinate Courts is regularly appraised by the Department Related 
Parliamentary Standing Committee and internal audit teams. In addition, the Scheme has been 
evaluated by third-party under the aegis of NITI Aayog at the time of extension of the Scheme. 
The latest third-party report inter-alia mentions that the Scheme demonstrates high relevance 
by strongly aligning its objective for infrastructure develop ment with national policies, 
sustainable development goals and the needs of its beneficiaries. Further, the report mentions 
that the districts with higher court room density have reported a 3 -8% decline in average case 
pendency and further highlighted that there is 16% reduction in case resolution time reducing 
from 3.1 years to 2.6 years in District Courts.

3236. SHRI SELVAM G 
 
SHRI C N ANNADURAI 
 
Will the Minister of AYUSH be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has reviewed the progress of AYUSH healthcare services for  
women in Tamil Nadu, particularly through the network of co -located AYUSH units under  
the National AYUSH Mission (NAM) in rural and coastal districts and if so, the details 
thereof; 
 
(b) the total number of women beneficiaries who have availed of AYUSH services relating to  
maternal and child health, anaemia management, adolescent health, menopause care and  
wellness during the last three years, district-wise; 
 
(c) whether the Government proposes to further strengthen the integration of AYUSH  
systems with public healthcare institutions in Tamil Nadu through Health and Wellness 
Centres, digital health initiatives and community outreach programmes; and 
 
(d) the additional measures planned to promote preventive healthcare, nutrition, mental  well-
being, yoga and holistic women's health through AYUSH interventions across Tamil Nadu,  
particularly in underserved districts? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE (IC) OF THE MINISTRY OF AYUSH 
 
(SHRI PRATAPRAO JADHAV) 
 
(a) Public Health being a State Subject, the primary responsibility to review the progress of 
Ayush healthcare services for women in Tamil Nadu, particularly through the network of co -
located Ayush units under the National Ayush Mission (NAM) in rural and coastal districts , 
lies with respective State Government. However, Ministry of Ayush  is regularly and 
vigorously monitoring the progress of implementation of various activities under National 
Ayush Mission (NAM) scheme through various methods as under:- 
 

2 
 
i. Collecting activity -wise physical/financial progress on regular interval from the 
State/UT Governments. 
ii. Conducting the field visits by central  team of the Ministry of Ayush, time to time, to 
analyse the actual progress of implementation of different activities for which State 
Government has reported expenditure and submitted utilization certificates. 
iii. Regional Review Meetings with State/UTs under the Chairmanship of Hon’ble 
Minister/Secretary to assess the implementation status and to decide way forward.  
iv. One to one meeting with States/UTs conducted for detailed review of physical and 
financial progress.  
v. Mid-term evaluation of NAM scheme implementation/progress by NITI Aayog 
through third party who undertakes field visits in State/UTs.  
 
Further, State Government of Tamil Nadu  reported that they regularly review the 
implementation and progress of A yush healthcare services in Tamil Nadu under NAM. The 
performance of Ayush healthcare services is reviewed every month by the District Siddha 
Medical Officers at the district level and periodically at the State level.  Under NAM, Ayush 
healthcare services for women are provided through a network of co -located Ayush units, 
Ayush Health & Wellness Centres [now known as Ayushman Arogya Mandir (Ayush)] , and 
Government Ayush institutions across the  State, including rural and coastal districts. At 
present, 94 co -located Ayush units (Annexure-I) are functioning in rural districts under 
NAM Scheme, 40 in rural coastal districts  (Annexure-II), and 16 in urban coastal districts 
under NAM  (Annexure-III). During last year, a total of 1,11,02,499 beneficiaries availed 
Ayush healthcare services through various Ayush health facilities in Tamil Nadu under NAM 
Scheme. Women -specific healthcare services, including maternal healthcare, are provided 
through various Ayush interventions. Under the Siddha system of medicine, the Magaperu 
Sanjeevi Scheme provides medicine kits to pregnant women, under which 1,27,084 pregnant 
women benefited during the last year. 
 
(b) As reported by State Government of Tamil Nadu, a  total of 3,47,112 women beneficiaries 
availed Ayush services relating to  maternal and child health, anaemia management, 
adolescent health, menopause care and  wellness during the last three years  under the 
Magaperu Sanjeevi Scheme . T he district -wise details of these women beneficiaries are 
enclosed as Annexure-IV.  
 
(c) As reported by State Government of Tamil Nadu,  650 Ayush Health & Wellness Centres 
[now known as Ayushman Arogya Mandir (Ayush)] across Tamil Nadu have been  
operationalized under the National Ayush Mission. Efforts are being made to further 
strengthen the integration of Ayush services with public healthcare institutions through 
digital health initiatives, including telemedicine and Health Management Information 
Systems (HMIS). Community outreach programmes, health awareness  camps, yoga sessions, 
wellness activities and preventive healthcare initiatives are being conducted regularly through 
Ayush institutions and Health & Wellness Centres.   
   
(d) As reported by the State of Tamil Nadu,  the Government is promoting preventive and 
holistic healthcare for women through AYUSH interventions across the State, including

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA
MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILYWELFARE
DEPARTMENTOF HEALTH AND FAMILYWELFARE
LOK SABHA
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3237
TO BE ANSWERED ON 7TH AUGUST 2026
IMPROVEMENT OF PRIMARY HEALTHCARE CENTRES IN MISHRIKH
†3237. SHRI ASHOK KUMAR RAWAT:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILYWELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) the current status regarding the improvement of Primary Healthcare Centres (PHCs) in the rural
areas of Mishrikh, Uttar Pradesh and the establishment of a major super-specialty hospital at the
district level for the treatment of critical illnesses;
(b) whether any assessment has been made regarding the estimated number of poor patients who
would benefit daily from the setting up of such hospitals;
(c) if so, the time by which the said hospitals are proposed to be set up along with the amount of
funds likely to be spent in this regard; and
(d) if not, the reasons therefor?
ANSWER
THE MINISTER OF STATEIN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILY
WELFARE
(SHRI PRATAPRAOJADHA V)
(a) to (d): ‘Public Health and Hospital’ is a State subject, the primary responsibility for planning,
implementing, maintaining and to set up adequate number of healthcare facilities as per requirement
is of that State Government. Under National Health Mission (NHM), financial and technical support
is provided to States/UTs to strengthen their healthcare system based on proposals received from
States/UTs in their Programme Implementation Plan (PIP) within their resource envelope.
As per the information provided by the State Government of Uttar Pradesh, health
services are provided at the Primary Health Centres (PHCs) operating under the Mishrikh
Development Block in Sitapur district in accordance with the resources available under the National
Health Mission and the schemes of the State Government. Necessary measures are taken to
strengthen buildings, equipment, medicines, human resources, and other basic infrastructure facilities.
As reported by the State Government of Uttar Pradesh, there is no separate detailed
assessment available regarding the estimated number of poor patients to be benefitted daily on
setting up of Super-Specialty hospital. However, the strengthening of healthcare facilities has been
ensured in Sitapur District so that all residents of the area, particularly patients from economically
weaker sections, are benefitted from quality healthcare services.
Further, as informed by the State Government, at present, no separate project has been
proposed for the establishment of a new hospital.

(c) & (d): The Law Commission, in its 120th Report  (1987), has recommended a judge -to-
population ratio of 50 judges per million of the Indian population.  Further, in 245th Report 
(2014), the Law Commission observed that filing of cases per capita varies substantially 
across geographical units as filings are associated with economic and social conditions of the 
population. As such the Law Commission did not consider the judge population ratio to be a 
scientific criterion for determining the adequacy of the judge strength in the country. The Law 
Commission found the “Rate of Disposal” method appropriate, which aims at the number of 
additional judges required to clear the backlog of cases and ensuring that new backlog is not 
created to be more pragmatic and useful. 
 
In August 2014, the Supreme Court asked the National Court Management System 
Committee (NCMS Committee) to examine the recommendations made by the Law 
Commission and to furnish its recommendations in this regard. NCMS Committee submitted 
its report to the Supreme Court in March, 2016. The Committee has proposed a “ weighted” 
disposal approach i.e. disposal weighted by the nature and complexity of cases in local 
conditions. As per the direction of the Hon’ble Supreme Court in its Order dated 02.01.2017, 
the Department of Justice has forwarded a copy of interim report of the NCMS Committee to 
all the State Governments and High Courts to enable them to take follow up action to 
determine the required strength of district and subordinate judiciary. 
 
(e): As per data available on the Nyaya Vikas Portal 2.0, as on 03.08.2026, the sanctioned 
strength of Judicial Officers  per million population (as per last census) in District & 
Subordinate Courts in Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh and the UT of Dadra & Nagar Haveli 
and Daman & Diu are as under: 
 
Sr. No. Name of State/UT Judges per million population 
1. Maharashtra 46.69 
2. Madhya Pradesh 28.24 
3. Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu 11.92 
 

3 
 
(f): Disposal of cases pending in various courts lies within the domain of the Judiciary. 
Disposal of cases in courts depends on several factors which, inter -alia, include availability 
of adequate number of Judges and Judicial officers, supporting court staff , physical 
infrastructure, complexity of facts involved, quality of investigation, nature of evidence, co-
operation of stake holders viz bar, investigation agencies, witnesses, litigants. However, the 
Government is fully committed for speedy disposal of cases and reducing pendency. The 
Government has taken several initiatives to provide an ecosystem for faster disposal of cases 
by the judiciary which, inter-alia, involves timely appointment of Judges, better infrastructure 
for courts including computerization, policy and legislative measures in the areas prone to 
excessive litigation, promoting Alternate Dispute Resolution mechanism, enactment and 
implementation of New Criminal Laws 2023, establishment of Fast Track Special Courts, re-
engineering of court procedure and emphasis on human resource development. 
 
Filling up of the vacancy in the higher Judiciary is a continuous, integrated and 
collaborative process between the executive and the judiciary. It requires consultation and 
approval from various Constitutional Authorities both at State and Central level w hich are 
obtained in accordance with the Memorandum of Procedure ( MoP). The recommendations 
also have to be considered in the light of such other reports as may be available to the 
Government in respect of the names under consideration. 
 
 Further, filling up of vacant positions of the judicial officers in District and 
Subordinate courts is the responsibility of the High Courts and State Governments concerned. 
As per the Constitutional framework, in exercise of powers conferred under the pr oviso to 
Article 309 read with Articles 233 and 234 of the Constitution, the respective State 
Government, in consultation with the High Court, frames the rules and regulations regarding 
the appointment and recruitment of Judicial Officers.  The Hon’ble Supreme Court vide order 
passed in January 2007 in the Malik Mazhar Sultan case, has inter -alia stipulated certain 
timelines, which are to be followed by the States and the respective High Courts for 
recruitment of judges in District and Subordinate Courts.
