GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS 
DEPARTMENT OF FERTILIZERS 
 
LOK SABHA 
 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3242 TO BE ANSWERED ON: 07.08.2026 
 
Shortage of DAP 
 
3242.   Shri Manickam Tagore B: 
            
   Will the Minister of Chemicals and Fertilizers be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether it is a fact that farmers are being forced to purchase alternative 
additional fertilizers due to shortage of DAP, if so, the details thereof along with the 
steps taken to ensure adequate availability of DAP during agricultural cropping 
seasons; 
 
(b) the details of fertilizer subsidy allocated, released and utilized for Urea and 
DAP during the last three years and the current financial year, along with its impact 
on retail prices for farmers, year-wise; 
 
(c) whether the Government proposes to increase domestic production capacity 
of Urea and DAP to reduce dependence on imports and ensure fertilizer security, if 
so, the details thereof; 
 
(d) whether any assessment has been conducted by the Government regarding 
the impact of Urea and DAP availability and prices on the cost of cultivation and 
farmers’ income, if so, the findings thereof; and 
 
(e) whether the Government has taken steps to improve fertilizer distribution 
through digital monitoring systems such as real-time tracking of stocks, movement 
and sales of Urea and DAP, if so, the details thereof? 
 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS & FERTILIZERS 
 
(SMT. ANUPRIYA PATEL) 
 
(a) to (e) Following steps are taken by the Government every season for ensuring 
timely and adequate availability of DAP and other fertilizers in the country: 
 
(i) Before the commencement of each cropping season, Department of Agriculture 
and Farmers Welfare (DA&FW), in consultation with all the State Governments, 
assesses the State-wise & month-wise requirement of fertilizers. On the basis of 
requirement projected by DA&FW, Department of Fertilizers (DoF) allocates 
adequate quantities of fertilizers to States by issuing monthly supply plan and 
continuously monitors the availability. 
 

(ii) The movement of all major subsidized fertilizers is monitored throughout the country 
by an on-line web-based monitoring system called integrated Fertilizer Management 
System (iFMS). 
 
(iii) The gap between demand (requirement) and production for Urea & other fertilizers 
is met through imports. The import for the season is also finalized well in advance 
to ensure timely availability.  
 
(iv) The State Governments are regularly advised to coordinate with manufacturers and 
importers for streamlining the supplies through timely placement of indents. 
 
(v) Regular coordination is done with the Ministry of Railways for giving sufficient rakes, 
priority to fertilizers and for timely evacuation of rakes for States. 
 
(vi) The distribution of fertilizers within the State at district/block level is done by the 
concerned State government. 
 
In view of above, the availability of DAP in the country has remained adequate during the 
ongoing Kharif 2026 season. The State-wise information regarding requirement, availability, 
sales and closing stock of DAP for the period  01.04.2026 to 03.08.2026 is placed at 
Annexure A. 
 
The details of total fertilizer subsidy allocated, disbursed during the last three years 
i.e. 2023-24 to 2025-26 and current financial year 2026-27 (as on 04.08.2026) by the 
Government is placed at Annexure B. 
Further, under the Urea Subsidy Scheme, Urea is provided to the farmers at a 
statutorily notified Maximum Retail Price (MRP). The MRP of 45 kg bag of urea is Rs.242 
per bag (exclusive of charges towards neem coating and taxes as applicable). The 
difference between the delivered cost of urea at farm gate and net market realization by the 
urea units is given as subsidy to the urea manufacturer/importer by the Government of India. 
Accordingly, all farmers are being supplied urea at the subsidized rate. 
With regard to Urea, the Government had announced New Investment Policy (NIP) – 
2012 on 2nd January, 2013 and its amendment on 7th October, 2014 to facilitate fresh 
investment in the urea sector and to make India self-sufficient in the urea sector. Total 6 new 
urea units have been set up under NIP-2012 which includes 4 urea units set up through Joint 
Venture Companies (JVC) of nominated PSUs and 2 urea units set up by the private 
companies. The units set up through JVC are Ramagundam urea unit of Ramagundam 
Fertilizers and Chemicals Ltd (RFCL) in Telangana and 3 urea units namely Gorakhpur, Sindri 
and Barauni of Hindustan Urvarak & Rasayan Limited (HURL) in Uttar Pradesh, Jharkhand 
and Bihar, respectively. The units set up by private companies are Panagarh urea unit of Matix 
Fertilizers and Chemicals Ltd. (Matix) in West Bengal; and Gadepan-III urea unit of Chambal 
Fertilizers and Chemicals Ltd. (CFCL) in Rajasthan. Each of these units has installed capacity 
of 12.7 Lakh Metric Tonne per annum (LMTPA). These units are highly energy efficient as they 
are based on latest technology. Therefore, these units have together added urea production 
capacity of 76.2 LMTPA, thereby total indigenous urea production capacity (Reassessed 
Capacity, RAC) has increased from 207.54 LMTPA during 2014-15 to 269.42 LMTPA during 
2026-27. Further, an exclusive policy for the revival of Talcher unit of FCIL through JVC of 
nominated PSUs namely Talcher Fertilizers Limited (TFL) by setting up a new Greenfield Urea 
plant of 12.7 LMTPA at coal gasification route has also been approved. Further, setting up of 
a new Brownfield Ammonia-Urea Complex named as Assam Valley Fertilizer and Chemical 
Company Ltd. (AVFCCL) with an annual capacity of 12.7 Lakh Metric Tonne of Urea through 

Joint Venture within the existing premises of Brahmaputra Valley Fertilizer Corporation Limited 
(BVFCL), Assam has been approved. These two projects are under execution phase. 
Also, the Government also notified the New Urea Policy (NUP) – 2015 on 25th May, 2015 for 
the existing 25 gas-based urea units with one of the objectives of maximizing indigenous urea 
production beyond RAC.  The NUP-2015 has led to additional production of urea by 20-25 LMT 
as compared to the production during 2014-15 annually.  
Above steps together have facilitated increase of Urea production from level of 225 LMT per 
annum during 2014-15 to a record Urea Production at 314.07 LMT during 2023-24. During 
2025-26, 293.30 LMT of Urea was produced in the country. 
 
In addition to this, on 15.07.2026, CCEA approved National Investment Policy for Urea-2026 
for Aatmanirbhar Bharat (NIPU-2026) for making fresh investments in Urea Sector. 
Further, the Government has implemented Nutrient Based Subsidy (NBS) Scheme w.e.f. 
01.04.2010 for Phosphatic and Potassic (P&K) Fertilizers. Under NBS Scheme, MRP of P&K 
fertilizers are decontrolled and companies are free to fix MRP as per their business dynamics 
at a reasonable level. The NBS subsidy is provided to manufacturer/importer on notified P&K 
fertilizers on its PoS sale during the season, depending on their nutrient content to ensure 
availability of fertilizers to farmers. The volatility in international prices of key fertilizers and raw 
materials is considered while fixing NBS rates for P&K fertilizers so that fertilizers remain 
affordable to the farmers. 
However, to make DAP being a key fertilizer, available at affordable price of Rs. 1350 per 50 
kg bag, special provisions like Rs. 3500 per MT to cover 'Other Costs' which includes costs 
incurred from factory gate to farm gate, advantage / disadvantage due to increase / decrease 
in international prices, provision for GST component included in the MRP and provision for 
reasonable return @ 4% of net MRP (MRP-GST) have been extended to both imported and 
domestic DAP and imported TSP over and above NBS subsidy for Kharif 2026 season to keep 
the prices of fertilizers stable. 
Under the NBS Scheme, P&K fertilizers are covered under Open General License (OGL) and 
companies are free to import/manufacture these fertilizers as per their business dynamics. 
However, to reduce dependence on imported Phosphatic fertilizers and make country self-
reliant   measures have been taken to encourage domestic production through guidelines 
18.01.2024 on reasonableness of MRP, wherein importers/ manufacturers and integrated 
manufacturers are given reasonable profit of 8%/10% and 12% respectively; based on the 
requests, the new manufacturing units or increase in manufacturing capacity of existing units 
have been recognized / taken on record under the NBS Scheme; the number of P&K fertilizers 
covered under NBS Scheme has increased from 22 grades in 2021 to 28 grades; Freight 
Subsidy on SSP, which is an indigenously manufactured fertilizer, is being provided since 
Kharif, 2022 to promote SSP usage for providing Phosphatic or 'P' nutrient to the soil. Further 
the rates of nutrients under NBS scheme are decided on biannual basis to ensure availability 
of fertilizers under the Scheme. 
*******

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA  
MINISTRY OF WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT  
 
LOK SABHA  
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3243  
ANSWERED ON 07.08.2026  
  
IMPLEMENTATION ASSESSMENT OF POSHAN TRACKER  
3243. SHRI KARTI P CHIDAMBARAM:  
Will the Minister of WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a)  whether the Government has undertaken any assessment of the implementation of the 
Poshan Tracker to evaluate its impact on delivery of nutrition and child development 
services under Saksham Anganwadi and POSHAN 2.0, if so, the details thereof;  
(b)  whether such assessment has identified any challenges relating to digital authentication, 
data quality/service delivery through Poshan Tracker, if so, the details thereof;  
(c)  whether the Government has prescribed any mechanism for periodic evaluation of the 
impact of the Poshan Tracker on beneficiary coverage and service delivery, if so, the 
details thereof; and 
(d)  the details of the measures taken/proposed to be taken to address the challenges 
identified and strengthen the implementation of the POSHAN Tracker?  
  
  
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT  
(SHRIMATI SAVITRI THAKUR)  
  
(a) to (d): To review the progress of the Mission Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0 digitally, 
the Ministry of Women and Child Development (MoWCD ) has introduced ‘Poshan Tracker’ 
application as an ICT based governance tool. It provides facility for monitoring and review of 
all services provided to the beneficiaries at Anganwadi Centres and also at their home. Poshan 
Tracker has enabled the Ministry , as well as States and UTs to continuously review the 
implementation of the Mission on various parameters and to make course correction.  
An outcome -based evaluation study of Mission Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0 was 
conducted by Development Monitoring and Evaluation Office  (DMEO), NITI Aayog (2025). 
As per the study, digitalization through Poshan Tracker Application has a multi -dimensional 
impact on nutrition monitoring, Early Childhood Care and Education (ECCE), beneficiary 
authentication, and service delivery efficiency. The Report highlighted Poshan Tracker as a 
significant shift from manual, paper -based systems to a technology -enabled governance 

framework under the Supplementary Nutrition Programme (SNP). As per the report, Poshan 
Tracker has become the cornerstone for digital monitoring of beneficiaries, inventory, and 
service delivery at Anganwadi Centres (AWCs). The expansion of digital platfor ms like the 
Poshan Tracker represents a foundational shift in governance, enabling greater responsiveness, 
efficiency, and transparency in the SNP’s last-mile delivery. Further, in pursuance to the Union 
Budget Speech of 2016, every scheme has been aligned  with the Finance Commission cycles 
and its continuation is based on the evaluation of scheme by a third party.  
To address network -related issues while using Poshan Tracker, such as low or no internet 
connectivity in some areas, the application provides offline functionality for conducting e-KYC 
and face matching under the Facial Recognition System (FRS) for distrib ution of Take-Home 
Ration (THR). OTP for e-KYC and Aadhar face matching has to be taken ONCE in the entire 
life cycle of a beneficiary. It creates ease of living for the beneficiaries to avail the Anganwadi 
services even when network or server issues are present. The data entered on the application in 
the offline mode has provision of 5 days to sync, once network restores.   
MoWCD provides continuous training and handholding support to Anganwadi Workers for 
effective use of the Poshan Tracker application through the following mechanisms:  
• Learning Videos and awareness documents: In the Resource section of the Poshan 
Tracker application, learning videos and awareness documents are available for 
Anganwadi Workers which can be accessed by them at any point of time for effective 
delivery of their routine tasks. 
• Under the Poshan Bhi Padhai Bhi (PBPB) initiative, the MoWCD  is imparting training 
to all the officials and field functionaries in the States and UTs through a cascading 
model of training, wherein Master Trainers (District Officers, Block Coordinators and 
Supervisors) are trained, and the master trainers further tr ain all Anganwadi Workers 
in the field. Training is imparted on different modules of Poshan Tracker, viz. Facial 
Recognition System (FRS), Geo -Tagging, Home Visit Scheduler etc. Block and 
District coordinators provide on -ground handholding support to AWWs and 
supervisors for effective usage of the Poshan Tracker Application and resolution of 
technical glitches. 
• Daily Virtual Classroom Sessions: Digital India Corporation (DIC) organises virtual 
classroom sessions every day (Monday to Friday) from 3:00 PM to 4:00 PM, in which 
Anganwadi Workers may join to raise operational queries and receive real -time 
clarifications on use of the application. Further, training sessions from 4:15 PM to 5:15 
PM for State officials (supervisor and above level) are organized to resolve 
implementation-related issues, disseminate updates, and provide training on newly 
introduced functionalities and enhancements in the Poshan Tracker application.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA
MINISTRY OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS
LOK SABHA
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO - 3244
ANSWERED ON - 07/08/2026
ARCTIC POLICY OF INDIA
3244. SHRI RAO RAJENDRA SINGH
Will the Minister of EXTERNAL AFFAIRS be pleased to state:-
(a) the measures taken by the Government under Arctic Policy of India to 
strengthen transportation and connectivity with the Nordic countries;
(b) the steps taken in coordination with the Nordic countries to mitigate  
climate change under India's Arctic Policy; and
(c) the manner in which India's partnership with the Nordic countries is  
strengthening maritime and environmental cooperation?

2
ANSWER
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS
(SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH)
(a) to (c) India’s Arctic Policy, titled “India and the Arctic: Building a  
Partnership for Sustainable Development”, was released in 2022. Guided  
by  the  Policy,  India  works  closely  with  all  the  Nordic  countries  on 
connectivity, climate action and maritime and environmental cooperation, 
including through Summit-level engagement.
At the 3 rd India-Nordic Summit, held in Norway on 19 May 2026, it  
was  decided  to  elevate  the  India-Nordic  relationship  to  a  Green 
Technology and Innovation Strategic Partnership. The leaders also agreed 
to improve connectivity between the Nordic and the Indo-Pacific regions, 
in line with the continued development of the India-Middle East-Europe  
Economic Corridor. There is also direct air connectivity with Finland and  
Denmark.
On climate change, India and the Nordic countries are working  
together on renewable energy, green hydrogen, zero- and low-emission  
technologies such as carbon capture, utilisation and storage and critical  
minerals in support of  the transition to clean energy and sustainable  
economic growth. The Leadership Group for Industry Transition (LeadIT),  

3
launched by India and Sweden in 2019 to reduce emissions from industry, 
has since been joined by most Nordic countries.
Maritime  and  environmental  cooperation  is  being  strengthened 
through  bilateral  dialogues  and  the  Indo-Pacific  Oceans  Initiative, 
covering maritime safety, welfare of seafarers, prevention of pollution at  
sea,  green  shipping,  shipbuilding,  sustainable  ship  recycling  and  
sustainable  management  of  ocean  resources.  India  has  recently  
commenced Maritime Security Dialogues with Nordic countries, including 
Norway and Denmark.
India also continues its scientific work in the Arctic through its  
research station, Himadri, in Svalbard, where winter expeditions have  
been undertaken since December 2023. India’s National Centre for Polar  
and Ocean Research collaborates with institutions in the Nordic countries 
to study changes in Arctic glaciers, ocean life and marine pollution.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA
MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILYWELFARE
DEPARTMENTOF HEALTH AND FAMILYWELFARE
LOK SABHA
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3245
TO BE ANSWERED ON 07.08.2026
CASES OF NIPAH VIRUS IN WEST BENGAL
3245. SHRI ASADUDDIN OWAISI:
Will the MINISTER OF HEALTH AND FAMILYWELFARE be pleased to state:-
(a) whether the Government is aware of the recent cases of Nipah virus outbreak reported in
West Bengal, with at least five confirmed cases and the existing of the virus in Kerala, if so,
the details thereof;
(b) the specific measures being taken by the Government to prevent the zoonotic transmission
from animals to humans, including the details of active surveillance in the affected regions;
(c) whether the Government has issued any advisory for the commencement of screening for
Nipah in containment zones across the country along with the details of critical care support
in this regard;
(d) the measures taken by the Government to contain the outbreak, given its high fatality rate
of 40 per cent to 75 per cent and the absence of approved vaccines or antivirals;
(e) whether a public health advisory has been issued to raise awareness about symptoms,
prevention and hygiene in the country, if so, the details thereof; and
(f) whether the Government is aware that Thailand and Singapore are screening passengers
arriving from West Bengal, if so, the details of the specific travel advisories issued for
outbound passengers from the affected regions?
ANSWER
THE MINISTER OF STATEIN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH & FAMILY
WELFARE
(SHRI PRATAPRAOJADHA V)
(a) to (e): The Government is aware of the reported cases of Nipah virus disease in the States
of West Bengal and Kerala. During 2026, West Bengal reported two laboratory-confirmed
cases of Nipah virus disease, including one death, while Kerala reported one laboratory-
confirmed case. All reported cases were promptly investigated by the respective State
Governments with technical support from the National Centre for Disease Control (NCDC).
National Joint Outbreak Response Teams (NJORTs) were deployed to both West Bengal and
Kerala to support epidemiological investigations, strengthen surveillance, facilitate contact
tracing, and assist the States in implementing appropriate public health measures for
containment of the outbreaks.
The details of the measures undertaken by the Government to prevent the zoonotic
transmission from animals to humans and to contain the outbreak are at Annexure.

The NCDC has developed and disseminated technical guidance documents, including
standard operating procedures, Learning Resource Packages and Communicable Disease
Alert to support uniform preparedness, surveillance, diagnosis and response across States and
Union Territories. The details may be seen on the links:
(https://ncdc.mohfw.gov.in/uploads/resource/1769335263_ZDPHI_Manual_2025_V2_06.11.
2025.pdf) and (https://ncdc.mohfw.gov.in/uploads/glimpse_pdfs/1770282425_CD-Alert-
NIPAH-Virus.pdf)
To strengthen risk communication and community awareness, NCDC has developed and
disseminated a range of Information, Education and Communication (IEC) materials,
including print, audio and video resources, on priority zoonotic diseases, including Nipah
Virus Disease. These materials are used for training of healthcare professionals as well as for
public awareness and community outreach activities. The details may be accessed at link:
https://ncdc.mohfw.gov.in/includes/Health_Information/healthcare.php
(f): The Government is aware that during the Nipah virus outbreak reported in West Bengal
in early 2026, Singapore and Thailand had introduced temporary public health screening,
including temperature screening, at airports and seaports for travellers arriving from the
affected areas in India. These measures were implemented for a limited period and were
subsequently discontinued.
*****

ANNEXURE
The control measures undertaken and contingency plans for prevention and
containment of Nipah virus disease outbreaks:
i. Ministry of Health & Family Welfare (MoHFW) maintained continued support and
collaborative engagement with both Virus Research and Diagnostic Laboratories
throughout the year, ensuring training, a steady supply of Personal protective equipment
and diagnostic reagents.
ii. Integrated Disease Surveillance Program (IDSP) mandates surveillance & response to
outbreak prone communicable diseases. IDSP plays a crucial role in prompt response and
surveillance of emerging and re-emerging diseases including Nipah Virus disease in the
country.
iii. Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) and ICMR- National Institute of Virology,
Pune, have strengthened Nipah surveillance by enhancing Acute Encephalitis Syndrome
in Kerala state and Severe Acute Respiratory Illness surveillance in West Bengal and
Kerala since October-November 2024.
iv. A comprehensive guideline on Nipah Virus has been prepared which can be accessed on
the link: https://ncdc.mohfw.gov.in/nipah-virus-guidelines/.
v. Under National One Health Programme for Prevention and Control of Zoonotic Diseases
(NOHP-PCZ) various initiatives are taken to strengthen prevention, detection, and
response capacities for zoonotic diseases in India, including Nipah Virus Disease.
vi. For institutionalization of One Health at National, State and district level – Zoonosis
committee have been formed in All States /UTs to review status of all zoonotic diseases
including Nipah virus
vii. NCDC has prepared a Technical Guidance on Zoonotic Disease, including Nipah Virus
Disease that may be accessed at link: https://ncdc.mohfw.gov.in/wp-
content/uploads/2024/04/Technical-Guidance-on-Zoonotic-Disease.pdf.
viii. Information,Education, and Communication(IEC) video onNipah virusdisease has
been prepared to create awareness in the public and prevent the spread of the disease. The
IEC may be accessed at link: https://ncdc.mohfw.gov.in/iec-material-on-zoonotic-disease-
nipah/.

V ACANCIESIN GOVERNMENT HOSPITALS AND MEDICAL COLLEGES
3246. MS. PRANITI SUSHILKUMAR SHINDE:
SHRI ARVIND GANPATSAWANT:
SHRI K RADHAKRISHNAN:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILYWELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) the total number of sanctioned posts and vacancies of specialists, doctors, nurses,
paramedical staff and faculty in Government hospitals and medical colleges and the number
of vacancies that have existed for more than one year across the country, State/UT-wise along
with the reasons therefor;
(b) whether the Government has identified critical shortages in specific specialities especially
in rural/underserved areas and if so, the details thereof;
(c) the steps taken by the Government to fill these vacancies including recruitment drives
undertaken during the last five years, contractual appointments, and incentives for service in
rural and remote areas; and
(d) whether any timeline has been fixed to address these vacancies and strengthen human
resources in public healthcare institutions and if so, the details thereof?
ANSWER
THE MINISTER OF STATEIN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND
FAMILYWELFARE
(SHRI PRATAPRAOJADHA V)
(a) to (d): Health is a State subject. The primary responsibility of strengthening public
healthcare system, including vacancies lies with the respective State/Union Territory
Governments. The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare provides technical and financial
support to the States/Union Territory to strengthen the public healthcare system in rural areas
based on the proposals received in the form of Programme Implementation Plans (PIPs)
under National Health Mission. Government of India provides approval for the proposal in
the form of Record of Proceedings (RoPs) as per norms & available resources.

The NHM supplements the regular human resources by filling up the gaps in human
resources in secondary and primary care facilities (District Hospital and below) as per Indian
Public Health Standards (IPHS).
The details of specialists, doctors, nurses and paramedical staff in Government
hospitals and their vacancies State/UT-wise can be accessed at the following link of HDI
2023-24:
https://www.mohfw-dohfw.gov.in/static/uploads/2026/05/57202cf30629539e4d0fb0a2f700ac
62.pdf
Under NHM, following types of incentives and honorarium are provided for encouraging
doctors and healthcare workers to practice in rural and remote areas of the country to mitigate
the impact of shortage of doctors and healthcare workers:
• Hard area allowance to specialist doctors for serving in rural and remote areas and for
their residential quarters so that they find it attractive to serve in public health
facilities in such areas.
• Honorarium to Gynaecologists/ Emergency Obstetric Care (EmOC) trained,
Pediatricians & Anesthetist/ Life Saving Anaesthesia Skills (LSAS) trained doctors is
also provided to increase availability of specialists for conducting Cesarean Sections
in rural & remote area.
• Incentives like special incentives for doctors, incentive for Auxiliary Nurse and
Midwife (ANM) for ensuring timely Antenatal Checkup (ANC) checkup and
recording, incentives for conducting Adolescent Reproductive and Sexual Health
activities.
• States are also allowed to offer negotiable salary to attract specialist including
flexibility in strategies such as “You Quote We Pay”.
• Non-Monetary incentives such as preferential admission in post graduate courses for
staff serving in difficult areas and improving accommodation arrangement in rural
areas have also been introduced under NHM.
• Multi-skilling of doctors is supported under NHM to overcome the shortage of
specialists. Skill upgradation of existing HR is another major strategy under NRHM
for achieving improvement in health outcomes.

The measures/steps taken by the Government to increase the doctors/medical
professionals in the country includes:-
• Centrally Sponsored Scheme for establishment of new medical college by upgrading
district/ referral hospital under which 157 medical colleges have been approved.
• Centrally Sponsored Scheme for strengthening/ upgradation of existing State
Government/Central Government Medical Colleges to increase MBBS and PG seats.
• DNB qualification has been recognized for appointment as faculty to take care of
shortage of faculty.
• Enhancement of age limit for appointment/ extension/ re-employment against posts of
teachers/Dean/Principal/ Director in medical colleges upto 70 years.
• Family Adoption Programme (FAP): The FAP has been incorporated into the MBBS
curriculum to provide equitable healthcare access to rural population. FAP involves
medical colleges adopting villages and MBBS students adopting families within these
villages. This enables regular follow-up of adopted families for vaccination, growth
monitoring, menstrual hygiene, Iron & Folic Acid (IFA) supplementation, healthy
lifestyle practices, nutrition, vector control, and medication adherence. It also helps in
educating families about ongoing government health programmes.
• District Residency Programme (DRP): The DRP notified by the NMC provides for
a compulsory three months posting cum training of PG medical students at District
Hospitals as a part of the course curriculum. DRP benefits the public by strengthening
healthcare delivery in rural and underserved areas.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF PORTS, SHIPPING & WATERWAYS 
 
LOK SABHA 
 UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3247  
ANSWERED ON 07.08.2026 
  
INDIAN SEAFARERS IN CONFLICT ZONES 
  
3247   SHRI V K SREEKANDAN: 
Will the Minister of PORTS, SHIPPING AND WATERWAYS be pleased to state: 
पȅन, पोत पįरवहन और जलमागŊ मंũी 
(a) whether it is true that the Directorate General of Shipping has advised maritime 
recruitment and placement agencies not to deploy Indian seafarers to conflict 
zones until further notice; 
(b) whether it is also true that these directives were issued after three Indian 
seafarers were killed and many were injured or missing in a U.S. strike on a 
ship off the coast of Oman;  
(c) whether it is also true that the Directorate General of Shipping is closely 
monitoring the evolving situation in coordination with all concerned in the light 
of continued attack on ships that carry Indian seafarers; and 
(d) if so, the details thereof? 
  
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF PORTS, SHIPPING & WATERWAYS 
(SHRI SARBANANDA SONOWAL) 
  
(a) to (d) In view of the evolving maritime security situation, the Directorate General of 
Maritime Administration (DGMA), a subordinate body under this Ministry progressively 
updates its advisories in response to the evolving security situation across the region. 
Advisories are precautionary in nature and are intended to enhance the safety and 
security of lndian seafarers. They were issued in response to the evolving security 
situation and not to any single incident.    
Further, from the onset of the security situation in the Strait of Hormuz, several 
measures have been taken to safeguard lndian seafarers. These include the 
establishment of a dedicated 24x7 Control Room, maintenance of a live vessel-and-
crew database, and issuance of a Situation Report (SITREP) every 24 hours (currently 
SITREP No. 165) to monitor the movement of vessels, lndian seafarers, incidents and 
casualties. DGMA has also developed an integrated digital platform with dedicated 
24x7 Marine Casualty Reporting, Crisis Management and Seafarer Grievance 
Redressal modules to ensure prompt reporting and response. The evolving maritime 

security situation is being continuously monitored through the DG Communication 
Centre (DGCOMM) in coordination with the Indian Navy, Flag States, coastal 
authorities, shipowners, ship managers, Recruitment and Placement Services Licence 
(RPSL) agencies and other concerned stakeholders. The details are placed at 
Annexure. 
   
  
  

Annexure 
  
(1)  Round-the-clock monitoring, reporting and crisis-response backbone 
  
(i)        DG Communication Centre (MMDAC) – the central maritime distress 
and coordination node, manned 24x7, together with a dedicated 24-hour 
Control Room.  
  
(ii)        Daily ship reporting advisory – vessels in the region report through the 
online Ship Reporting Form, maintaining a live vessel-and-crew database. 
  
(iii)       Continuous real-time monitoring – through the DGComm Centre, with a 
Situation Report issued every 24 hours (currently SITREP No. 165) to track 
vessels, seafarers, incidents and casualties. 
  
(iv)      eNavik Portal – an integrated digital platform with dedicated 24x7 Marine 
Casualty Reporting, Crisis Management and Seafarer Grievance Redressal 
modules, providing digital incident reporting with automated routing to the 
concerned authorities and real-time tracking of response measures. 
  
(2)       Whole-of-government and international coordination 
  
(i)        Inter-agency coordination is maintained by DGMA/ Ministry of Ports, 
Shipping & Waterways with the Ministry of External Affairs, the Indian Navy, the 
Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas, the Department of Fertilizers, the IFC-IOR 
and Indian Missions abroad. 
  
(ii)    International coordination – evacuation of stranded seafarers is pursued 
through a coordinated mechanism involving the IMO, the UKMTO, the MICA 
Centre and coastal States. 
  
  
(3)       Evacuation and repatriation 
As on 03 August 2026, 4052 seafarers have been repatriated from the Gulf 
region and 62 vessels have successfully transited Strait of Hormuz (23 Indian-
flagged and 39 foreign-flagged) for India. 
  
(4)      RPSL / e-migration system 
 
Single point of control – every Indian seafarer is engaged through a licensed 
RPSL agency and cannot clear e-migration or sign on to a vessel without 
formal, verified approval.  
  
(5)       Welfare and Assistance 
i. Family support – close and continuing contact with the families of 
affected seafarers is maintained. 
ii. Compensation in fatality cases – immediate support including release of 
Rs. 10,00,000 through the Seafarers Welfare Fund Society. 

iii. 24x7 grievance redressal – multiple always-on channels for assistance 
domestic toll-free 1800-889-7768; international toll-free (USA) +1-888-
988-0256; WhatsApp +91 8655856830; email enavik.24x7@gov.in; and 
the e-Navik grievance portal. 
  
(6)   Advisories to Ensure the Safety and Security of Indian Seafarers: 
i. DGS Advisory (14.01.2026) – Advisory to Indian Seafarers and Shipping 
Stakeholders in view of MEA Advisory on Iran, advising shipping companies 
not to deploy Indian seafarers to Iran until further orders, requiring close 
monitoring of Indian crews in the region, and directing seafarers to follow 
advisories issued by the Embassy of India and the Ministry of External Affairs. 
ii. DGS Circular 09 of 2026 (28.02.2026) – Urgent Advisory to Indian Seafarers 
and Shipping Stakeholders in view of Escalating Situation in Iran, requiring 
Indian seafarers in Iran to remain vigilant, register with the Embassy of India, 
coordinate for safe departure where feasible, and directing stakeholders to 
immediately provide details of Indian seafarers in affected areas. 
iii. DGS Circular 10 of 2026 (06.03.2026) – Safety Advisory for Indian Seafarers 
and Shipping Stakeholders Operating in the Persian Gulf, Strait of Hormuz and 
Adjacent Waters, advising continuous vigilance, compliance with ISPS Code 
security measures, establishment of 24x7 emergency contact mechanisms, 
liaison with Indian Missions, emergency preparedness, and psychological 
counselling support for seafarers and their families where necessary. 
iv. DGS Circular 11 of 2026 (07.03.2026) – Social Media Advisory to Maritime 
Stakeholders and Seafarer Community, directing maritime stakeholders to 
refrain from circulating unverified information, rumors, fake videos or 
speculative reports and to rely only on authenticated information from official 
sources. 
v. DGS Circular 21 of 2026 (07.04.2026) – Safety Advisory for Indian Seafarers 
Ashore in Iranian Ports and Onboard Vessels Operating in or Around Iranian 
Waters, advising seafarers in Iran to remain at designated locations, avoid 
unnecessary travel, maintain heightened vigilance, follow Embassy advisories 
and remain in contact with company representatives, while also providing 24×7 
emergency assistance contact details. 
vi. DGS Circular 31 of 2026 (13.06.2026) – Precautionary Measures for Indian 
Seafarers in view of the Heightened Security Situation in the Gulf Region, 
reiterating heightened security vigilance, directing shipping companies and 
RPSL companies to restrict deployment of Indian seafarers to conflict areas 
until further orders (except emergency crew changes with consent), monitoring 
and reporting requirements, and dissemination of verified security information. 
vii. DGS Circular No. 36 of 2026 {15.07.2026) : In view of renewed attacks on 
merchant vessels, DGS Circular No. 36 of 2026 mandated the implementation 
of full International Ship and Port Facility Security (ISPS) Code security 
measures and advised against the deployment of Indian seafarers on voyages 
transiting through the gulf region. 
viii. DGMA Circular No.41 of 2026 (23.07.2026) – Advisory issued for Indian and 
foreign flagged vessels carrying Indian seafarers operating in the Black Sea, 

requiring enhanced caution, voyage specific security assessments, strict 
adherence to security advisories and immediate reporting of incidents. 
ix. DGS Circular No.42 of 2026 (23.07.2026) - Advisory issued for vessels 
operating in the Bab-el-Mandeb Strait, Southern Red and adjoining Yemen 
waters, directing shipowners and masters to exercise utmost caution, 
continuous monitor security, developments and implement additional risk 
mitigation measures.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA
MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILYWELFARE
DEPARTMENTOF HEALTH AND FAMILYWELFARE
LOK SABHA
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. †3248

HEALTH INFRASTRUCTURE PROJECTS IN BAREILY
†3248. SHRI CHHATRAPALSINGH GANGWAR:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILYWELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) the present status of the health infrastructure projects sanctioned under the Pradhan Mantri
Ayushman Bharat Health Infrastructure Mission (PM-ABHIM) and other Central Government
health schemes in Uttar Pradesh, particularly in Bareilly district;
(b) the details of the progress made and the expenditure incurred so far under the said projects;
(c) whether any additional proposal is under consideration by the Government for the further
strengthening of the tertiary healthcare services and medical infrastructure in Bareilly division;
and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
ANSWER
THE MINISTER OF STATEIN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND
FAMILYWELFARE
(SHRI PRATAPRAOJADHA V)
(a) to (d): Pradhan Mantri Ayushman Bharat Health Infrastructure Mission (PM-ABHIM), a
Centrally Sponsored Scheme (CSS) with certain Central Sector (CS) components, has been
implemented to strengthen India's public health system through reforms that integrate health service
delivery, public health action and health research, thereby enhancing the capacity of public health
systems to effectively respond to pandemics and other public health emergencies.
Under the CSS component of the scheme, administrative approvals have been accorded to
Uttar Pradesh for construction/strengthening and establishment of 1670 Building-less Sub Health
Centre–Ayushman Arogya Mandirs (SHC-AAMs), 674 Urban Ayushman Arogya Mandirs (U-
AAMs), 515 Block Public Health Units (BPHUs), 75 Integrated Public Health Laboratories
(IPHLs) and 74 Critical Care Blocks (CCBs).
As per the information provided by the Government of Uttar Pradesh, in Bareilly district,
one Integrated Public Health Laboratory (IPHL) and ten Block Public Health Units (BPHUs) and

15 Sub-Health Centre- Ayushman Arogya Mandirs (SHC- AAMs) have been approved under PM-
ABHIM.
Under PM-ABHIM, funds are released to States/Union Territories on a lump-sum basis
based on approved activities, enabling them to utilize the funds as per their assessed needs and
priorities. The details of Central Release and Expenditure under PM-ABHIM to Uttar Pradesh for
the last three financial years i.e. from FY 2023-24 to FY 2025-26 is as under:
(Rs. in Crores)
State 2023-24 2024-25 2025-26

Note:
1. The above releases relate to Central Govt. Grants & do not include State share contribution.
2. Expenditure includes expenditure against Central Release, State release & unspent balances at the beginning of the year.
3. Expenditure is as per FMRs submitted by States/UTs and is provisional.
The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare provides technical and financial support to the
States/UTs including Uttar Pradesh to strengthen the public healthcare system in rural areas based
on the proposals received in the form of Programme Implementation Plans (PIPs) under National
Health Mission. Government of India provides approval for the proposal in the form of Record of
Proceedings (RoPs) as per norms & available resources. Details of the approvals given for the
strengthening healthcare in Uttar Pradesh are available at website of Ministry of Health and Family
Welfare at the Uniform Resources Locator (URL) as under:
www.nhm.gov.in/index4.php?lang=1&level=0&linkid=49&lid=62
The Pradhan Mantri Swasthya Suraksha Yojana (PMSSY) aims at correcting regional
imbalances in the availability of affordable tertiary healthcare services and to augment facilities for
quality medical education in the country. Under the Scheme, approvals has been accorded to Uttar
Pradesh for Establishment of 2 new All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS) at Raebareli &
Gorakhpur and upgradation of four Government Medical Colleges/ Institutions (GMCIs) viz.
SGPGIMS, Lucknow; Trauma Centre (TC) in Institute of Medical Sciences (IMS), BHU, Varanasi;
Jawaharlal Nehru Medical College of Aligarh Muslim University (AMU), Aligarh; Govt. Medical
College, Jhansi; BRD Medical College, Gorakhpur; MLN Medical College, Allahabad; LLRM
Medical College, Meerut; Government Medical College, Agra; Government Medical College,
Kanpur; SSB at Institute of Medical Sciences (IMS), BHU, Varanasi; and RIO, IMS, BHU,

Varanasi.
Under Centrally Sponsored Scheme (CSS) for ‘Establishment of new medical colleges
attached with existing district/referral hospitals’ with preference to underserved areas and
aspirational districts, where there is no existing Government or private medical college. 27 medical
colleges were approved in Uttar Pradesh State at Districts Basti; Faizabad; Firozabad;

Deoria; Ghazipur; Mirzapur; Bijnaur; Kushinagar; Sultanpur; Gonda; Lalitpur; LakhimpurKheri;
Chandauli; Bulandshahar; Sonbhadra; Pilibhit; Auraiya; Kanpur Dehat; Kaushambi and Amethi.

 UNSTARRED QUESTION NO: 3249

FACILITIES IN ANGANWADIS  
  
3249. SHRI VARUN CHAUDHRY : 
  
Will the Minister of WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT  be pleased to state:  
(a) the total number of operational Anganwadi Centres (AWCs) and the number of AWCs 
which lack the facilities of drinking water, toilets, electricity connection, etc.; and  
(b) the time frame by which the facilities like drinking water, toilets, electricity connection etc. 
will be provided in the AWCs across the country?  
  
ANSWER 
  
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT  
(SHRIMATI SAVITRI THAKUR)  
  
(a) to (b) The state wise number of Anganwadi Centres (AWCs) and details of infrastructure 
are available at the link: https://www.poshantracker.in/statistics.  
Mission Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0 is a Centrally Sponsored scheme. The 
implementation of the scheme falls under the ambit of State Governments and UTs 
administration. The matter regarding infrastructure is regularly taken up with States and UTs 
through sustained engagements and video conferences so as to ensure uninterrupted delivery 
of services to the beneficiaries.  
Also, in order to improve the infrastructure facilities at AWCs, funds @Rs.17,000/ - for 
providing drinking water facilities and @Rs.36,000/- for construction of toilets are provided to
